Debuting Mazda's SKYACTIV powertrain suite and Kodo 'Soul of Motion' design language, the CX-5 elevated the mid-size family crossover segment with class-leading steering feel, premium interiors, and punchy turbo power.

featured_models.name: G-Class (Geländewagen)
featured_models.overview: The immortal Mercedes-Benz Geländewagen. Originating as a relentless military off-roader with three locking differentials, the G-Class became a trusted explorer in the Australian outback and was selected by the Australian Defence Force under Project Overlander Land 121, resulting in over 2,000 bespoke Australian Army 4x4 and 6x6 vehicles. Concurrently, the civilian W463 morphed into the ultimate status symbol through the roaring twin-turbo V8 AMG G63.

featured_models.name: Lancer Evolution & Ralliart
featured_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution and Ralliart models represent one of the greatest chapters in modern Australian performance car folklore. Born directly from World Rally Championship battles where Tommi Mäkinen claimed four consecutive WRC drivers' titles, the Evo delivered staggering turbocharged all-wheel-drive grip, Active Yaw Control (AYC), and giant-killing cross-country pace.

featured_models.name: Jimny / Sierra / Stockman
featured_models.overview: The Suzuki Jimny, Sierra, and Stockman represent Australia's most revered lightweight, go-anywhere 4WD institution. Defying its miniature dimensions with a genuine ladder-frame chassis, dual-range transfer case, and live beam axles front and rear, it has conquered the Simpson Desert, Victorian High Country, and outback cattle stations for half a century.

featured_models.name: Kluger
featured_models.overview: The Toyota Kluger (sold globally as the Highlander) is Australia's quintessential car-based 7-seat family crossover SUV. Blending passenger-car ride comfort with cavernous interior room, powerful V6 and hybrid powertrains, and all-weather AWD assurance, it became a cornerstone of Australian suburban family motoring.

featured_models.name: Polo
featured_models.overview: Volkswagen's premium compact hatchback in Australia. Across four generations from the 6N to the modern MQB AW, the Polo brought big-car refinement, solid German safety, and pocket-rocket performance through the beloved Polo GTI.

featured_models.name: Tiguan
featured_models.overview: Volkswagen's powerhouse medium SUV in Australia, delivering European road manners, turbocharged TSI petrol and TDI diesel powertrains, 4Motion all-wheel drive, spacious 5-seat and 7-seat Allspace layouts, and the blisteringly fast 235kW Tiguan R.

featured_models.name: Q5 & SQ5
featured_models.overview: Audi's best-selling luxury SUV in Australia. Built on the longitudinal MLB platform with quattro permanent all-wheel drive, the Q5 balanced executive prestige with family versatility, while the twin-turbo diesel SQ5 BiTDI became an unprecedented cult sales sensation in Australia.

featured_models.name: Ford Ranger
featured_models.overview: The Ford Ranger is Australia's best-selling vehicle and one of the country's crowning engineering triumphs. Designed, engineered, and developed from the ground up by Ford Australia's 2,000-strong engineering and design team at Campbellfield, Victoria and the You Yangs Proving Ground, the Ranger is exported to over 180 countries. Across the PJ/PK, the revolutionary T6 (PX I, II, III), and the Next-Gen (PY), the Ranger redefined dual-cab refinement, off-road ability, and high-speed off-road performance through the bespoke Ranger Raptor.

featured_models.name: Holden Captiva
featured_models.overview: The Holden Captiva was Holden's core mid-size family SUV between 2006 and 2018, competing in Australia's exploding SUV segment against the Ford Territory and Toyota Kluger. Built on GM's global Theta platform, the range uniquely comprised two distinct body styles: the 5-seater Captiva 5 (Opel Antara twin) and the 7-seater Captiva 7 (Chevrolet Captiva). Over 150,000 Captivas found homes in Australian driveways thanks to keen pricing, standard three-row seating, AWD capability, and Australian-built Alloytec 3.2L and 3.0L SIDI V6 engines alongside 2.0L and 2.2L common-rail turbo diesels. Series II arrived in 2011 with refreshed styling, before the model was replaced by the Equinox and Acadia.

featured_models.name: Holden Jackaroo
featured_models.overview: The Holden Jackaroo (Isuzu Trooper / Bighorn) was Holden's frontline heavy-duty four-wheel-drive wagon from 1981 to 2004. Engineered to conquer the Australian outback, the Jackaroo competed directly against the Toyota LandCruiser Prado, Mitsubishi Pajero, and Nissan Patrol. The first-generation UBS-1 (1981-1992) offered short and long wheelbase bodies with rugged four-cylinder petrol and diesel engines. The second-generation UBS-2 (1992-2004) expanded into a wide-body luxury family 4WD featuring coil-sprung rear suspension, shift-on-the-fly 4WD, potent 3.2L and 3.5L DOHC 24V V6 petrol engines (158 kW), and advanced 3.0L 4JX1 common-rail turbo-diesel. The flagship Monterey added leather trim, woodgrain, climate control, and heated seats.

featured_models.name: D-MAX
featured_models.overview: The Isuzu D-MAX is an Australian commercial and recreational ute powerhouse. Renowned for its commercial truck-derived 3.0-litre 4JJ-series turbo diesel engine, 3,500kg braked towing capacity, and unbreakable durability, the D-MAX grew from an independent newcomer in 2008 into the third best-selling vehicle outright in Australia.

featured_models.name: Grand Cherokee
featured_models.overview: The American flagship that revolutionized Australia's large SUV market. Across five generations (ZJ, WJ, WK, WK2, and WL), the Grand Cherokee blended authentic Jeep trail capability with luxury appointments, muscular HEMI V8s, efficient 3.0L diesels with 3,500kg towing, and the earth-shattering 522kW Grand Cherokee Trackhawk.

featured_models.name: Range Rover & Discovery
featured_models.overview: The twin benchmarks of British luxury and all-terrain expedition mastery in Australia. The Range Rover created the luxury 4WD genre in 1972, proving that supreme off-road capability could coexist with peerless aristocratic comfort. The Land Rover Discovery launched in Australia in 1991, democratizing Range Rover technology into an iconic stepped-roof, 7-seat family adventurer.

featured_models.name: RX-3 / 808
featured_models.overview: The Mazda RX-3 (Savanna) and its reciprocating-piston sister the Mazda 808 (Grand Familia) are iconic pillars of Australian motorsport history and Japanese performance folklore. Famed for taking the fight directly to Holden Torana GTR XU-1s and Ford Falcon GT-HOs at Mount Panorama Bathurst, the RX-3's screaming twin-rotor Wankel rotary engine won legions of fanatical followers.

featured_models.name: Starion & Cordia Turbo
featured_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Starion Turbo and Cordia GSR Turbo were the trailblazers of Japanese factory turbocharging in 1980s Australia. From the front-wheel drive Cordia GSR with its mind-bending 'Super Shift' 4x2 twin-stick dual-range transmission to the widebody, rear-wheel drive Starion Turbo that battled Australian Touring Cars in Group E and Group A, these coupes created Australia's turbo street-racing legend.

featured_models.name: Triton
featured_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Triton has been one of Australia's favourite dual-cab utes for over four decades, offering tough ladder-chassis capability, advanced Super Select II 4WD, and exceptional value for trades and families.

featured_models.name: Cayenne & Macan
featured_models.overview: The commercial lifeblood of modern Porsche. When introduced in 2003, the Cayenne proved that a true Porsche could haul five adults and conquer the Simpson Desert, while setting racetrack lap records. The smaller Macan arrived in 2014, quickly becoming Porsche's best-selling model in Australia, and leading Porsche's electric transformation with the Macan EV.

featured_models.name: Amarok
featured_models.overview: Volkswagen's rugged mid-size commercial pickup truck, celebrated in Australia for full-time 4Motion all-wheel drive, class-leading tub width capable of carrying a full-sized Australian pallet between the wheel arches, and powerhouse 3.0-litre V6 TDI engines developed with Walkinshaw Automotive (W580).

featured_models.name: Giulia Sprint GT, GTV & Giulia Quadrifoglio
featured_models.overview: The passionate soul of Italian motoring in Australia. Spanning from the Bertone-styled 105 Series Giulia Sprint GT and Bathurst-winning 1750/2000 GTV, through the transaxle Alfetta GTV6 Group A touring car, to the spine-tingling Busso V6 156 GTA and the modern Giorgio-platform Giulia Quadrifoglio with its Ferrari-derived 375kW twin-turbo V6.

featured_models.name: 500 & Abarth 595/695
featured_models.overview: The Italian style icon that charmed Australia. From the original rear-engined 500 'Bambino' that motorized post-war migrants and Australian urbanites, to the retro-chic 2008 rebirth (Typ 312) and the scorpion-badged Abarth 595 and 695 hot hatches with screaming Record Monza exhausts and Brembo brakes.

featured_models.name: Ford Everest
featured_models.overview: While built at AutoAlliance Thailand in Rayong, the Ford Everest was conceived, designed, engineered, and durability-tested in Australia by Ford's 2,000-strong global product development hub at Campbellfield and the You Yangs Proving Ground. Developed concurrently with the Ranger ute, the Everest transformed the T6 ladder-frame architecture into a refined 7-seat family wagon featuring coil-sprung Watt's linkage rear suspension, electronic terrain management, and 3.1-tonne towing. The 2015 UA series launched with the rugged 3.2L 5-cylinder Duratorq turbo-diesel and later 2.0L Bi-Turbo with 10-speed auto. The 2022+ UB Next-Gen Everest elevated the platform into an opulent, class-leading 4WD with standard 3.5-tonne towing and a flagship 3.0L V6 Turbo Diesel producing 184 kW and 600 Nm.

featured_models.name: Wrangler
featured_models.overview: The direct descendant of the WWII Willys military Jeep, celebrated in Australia for live beam axles, removable doors and roof, fold-flat windscreen, and rock-crawling Rubicon mastery across TJ, JK, and JL generations.

featured_models.name: T60 & eT60
featured_models.overview: The Chinese 1-tonne ute that disrupted the Australian market. Debuting in 2017 as the first Chinese-manufactured vehicle to achieve a 5-star ANCAP safety rating, the LDV T60 delivered unmatched equipment-for-price value. The 2021 T60 Max raised the stakes with a class-leading 160kW/500Nm 2.0L Bi-Turbo diesel, while the 2022 eT60 became Australia's first commercially available electric factory ute.

featured_models.name: RX-7
featured_models.overview: The Mazda RX-7 is a rotary-powered sports car legend with deep Australian motorsport roots. From Allan Moffat's ATCC championship and Bathurst battles in the 1980s to Mazda Motorsport's Australian-exclusive RX-7 SP winning the Bathurst 12 Hour in 1995.

featured_models.name: C-Class
featured_models.overview: Mercedes-Benz's most popular luxury nameplate in Australia, spanning W202, W203, W204, W205, and W206. Renowned for supreme safety engineering, quiet cabin isolation, and thundering naturally aspirated and biturbo V8 AMG performance flagships.

featured_models.name: ZS / ZST / MG4
featured_models.overview: The modern pillars of MG Motor's Australian volume resurgence under SAIC: the top-selling ZS and turbocharged ZST compact SUVs, the trailblazing ZS EV, and the universally acclaimed rear-wheel-drive MG4 electric hatchback (including the 320kW XPower).

featured_models.name: Pajero
featured_models.overview: With 12 victories in the grueling Dakar Rally, the Mitsubishi Pajero is one of the world's most successful four-wheel drives. In Australia, it defined the family 4WD wagon for nearly four decades across four generations.

featured_models.name: 205, 306, 208 & 308 GTi
featured_models.overview: The aristocrats of French hot hatch engineering. For more than three decades in Australia, Peugeot's GTi lineage defined what a front-wheel drive performance car could achieve. From the featherweight, razor-sharp 205 GTi 1.9 that reset international benchmarks, through the passive rear-steering 306 GTi-6 with its class-first six-speed manual, to the Peugeot Sport-engineered 308 GTi 270 with Torsen LSD and massive Alcon brakes.

featured_models.name: Jumbuck & Satria (including Satria GTi)
featured_models.overview: The cult Malaysian heroes of Australian roads. The Proton Satria GTi became an instant hot hatch sensation in 1999, engineered with genuine Lotus suspension wizardry, Recaro bucket seats, riveted widebody arch flares, and a twin-cam Mitsubishi engine. Alongside it, the Proton Jumbuck carved out a unique niche from 2003 as Australia's most affordable brand-new ute, offering compact car economy with a half-tonne payload.

featured_models.name: Clio RS & Megane RS (Renault Sport)
featured_models.overview: The front-wheel-drive Nurburgring lap record conquerors. Developed by the wizards of Renault Sport at Dieppe, the Clio RS and Megane RS established an unbeatable pedigree in Australia for pure driving dynamics, PerfoHub independent steering axis suspension, mechanical limited-slip differentials, and Brembo stopping power.

Born from jets. Saab brought Swedish aircraft engineering, wraparound windscreens, night panels, and turbocharging mastery to Australia across more than three decades. The Classic 900 Turbo established Saab's intellectual cool, followed by the lightning-quick 9-3 Viggen and the 206kW 2.8T Aero V6.

featured_models.name: Octavia
featured_models.overview: The intelligent family choice in Australia. Since spearheading Skoda's return to Australia in October 2007, the Octavia has won legions of loyal fans by combining Volkswagen Group engineering and Golf GTI drivetrains with cavernous boot space and 'Simply Clever' practical details. The Octavia RS Liftback and Combi wagon represent Australia's favorite value performance family express.

featured_models.name: Model 3
featured_models.overview: The electric vehicle that opened the floodgates for mass EV adoption in Australia. Built in Shanghai for the Australian market, the Model 3 transformed automotive sales by outselling traditional petrol luxury sedans like the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes C-Class.

featured_models.name: RAV4
featured_models.overview: The Toyota RAV4 created the compact car-based recreational SUV category in 1994. Across five generations, it grew into Australia's favourite SUV, with the XA50 Hybrid triggering unprecedented multi-month waitlists.

featured_models.name: Shark 6 / Atto 3 / Seal
featured_models.overview: The trio of game-changing vehicles that propelled BYD to electric and hybrid leadership in Australia: the Atto 3 compact SUV, the Seal sports sedan, and the groundbreaking Shark 6 plug-in hybrid dual-cab ute with 321kW.

featured_models.name: Cannon / Haval H6 / Tank 300
featured_models.overview: The full evolution of Great Wall Motor in Australia: beginning with the pioneering 2009 Great Wall V240 and V200 utes, progressing to the top-selling GWM Cannon dual-cab, high-tech Haval H6 Hybrid SUV, and heavy-duty Tank 300 off-roader.

featured_models.name: Stinger
featured_models.overview: The Kia Stinger arrived in Australia in late 2017 just as Holden and Ford ceased local manufacturing, instantly becoming the spiritual successor to the rear-wheel-drive Falcon and Commodore. Powered by a 272kW twin-turbo V6, it was adopted by Australian police forces as a high-speed pursuit interceptor.

featured_models.name: BT-50
featured_models.overview: The Mazda BT-50 has been an Australian tradie, touring, and towing mainstay across three generations, moving from a Ford Ranger twin with 3.2L 5-cylinder power to an Isuzu D-Max platform with the 3.0L 4JJ3 turbo-diesel.

featured_models.name: Model Y
featured_models.overview: Australia's top-selling electric SUV and one of the highest-selling SUVs outright in Australia. Built on the Model 3 platform with a taller crossover body, 2,158 litres of total cargo storage, and class-leading electrical efficiency.

featured_models.name: 86 / GR86
featured_models.overview: The Toyota 86 and GR86 re-energized accessible rear-wheel-drive sports motoring in Australia. Developed jointly with Subaru (who built the cars at the Gunma Main Plant), the 86 combined a low center of gravity boxer engine, lightweight chassis, razor-sharp steering, and rear-drive dynamics at an accessible price point.

featured_models.name: Holden Colorado
featured_models.overview: The Holden Colorado was Holden's rugged 4x4 and 4x2 dual-cab, space-cab, and single-cab workhorse pick-up, replacing the legendary Rodeo in 2008. Across the RC and RG generations, the Colorado delivered class-leading 3.5-tonne braked towing capacity and up to 500Nm of torque from its Duramax 2.8L turbo-diesel engine. In 2016, Holden's engineering team at Lang Lang conducted a massive Australian-specific chassis, steering, and powertrain calibration that transformed refinement and dynamics.

all_models.name: Holden Commodore
all_models.overview: The Holden Commodore was Australia's definitive full-size passenger car, holding the crown as the nation's best-selling car for 15 consecutive years (1996-2010). Spanning 16 distinct series codes across five generations from the original 1978 VB to the billion-dollar Australian-engineered VE/VF Zeta platform and the imported European ZB, the Commodore was the family hauler, police highway patrol interceptor, commercial utility, and Mount Panorama Bathurst racing champion for over four decades.

all_models.name: Holden Kingswood / Belmont / Premier
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Wagon / Utility / Panel Van / Cab Chassis
all_models.overview: The Holden Kingswood was Australia's definitive full-size family car and commercial workhorse from 1968 to 1985. Replacing the HR series with the all-new HK, the Kingswood moniker became an indelible piece of Australian cultural lexicon—celebrated in television ('Kingswood Country'), song, and outback folklore. Encompassing the budget Belmont, mainstream Kingswood, luxury Premier, sporty Monaro-derived options, surf-culture Sandman van/ute, and heavy-duty One Tonner cab-chassis, over 1.5 million examples were produced across HK, HT, HG, HQ, HJ, HX, HZ, and WB series.

all_models.name: Ford Falcon
all_models.overview: The Ford Falcon is one of the most storied names in Australian industrial and cultural history. Manufactured continuously at Broadmeadows, Victoria for 56 years (1960-2016) across seven distinct generations and over 3.5 million units, the Falcon fought an epic rivalry with the Holden Commodore. From the pioneering XK and the legendary XY GT-HO Phase III (the fastest 4-door production car in the world) to the Australian-designed XA hardtop, the bestselling XF, the indestructible Intech and Barra DOHC sixes, the high-revving Boss V8s, and the supercharged Sprint series, the Falcon embodied Australian engineering resilience and high performance.

all_models.name: Holden Astra
all_models.overview: Spanning 36 years across seven generations, the Holden Astra was Holden's frontline small car. Launched in August 1984 as the LB/LC Astra, it originated as a badge-engineered Nissan Pulsar assembled in Clayton, Victoria. Under the Button Car Plan, the 1987 LD Astra combined Nissan body engineering with Holden's locally manufactured 1.6L and 1.8L Family II engines. In 1996, the Astra was reborn as the TR series, imported from Opel in Europe. The 1998 TS Astra became a massive commercial triumph, winning Wheels Car of the Year and spawning the hot hatch SRi and SRi Turbo (147 kW). The 2004 AH brought dynamic European styling and the 177 kW Astra VXR, followed by the PJ VXR coupe and the final high-tech 2016-2020 BK Astra hatchback (European Car of the Year) before Holden's retirement.

all_models.name: Holden EJ / EH / HD / HR
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Utility / Panel Van
all_models.overview: The 1962-1968 era represents the golden age of 1960s Holden dominance. The July 1962 EJ introduced clean, modern European-inspired styling, the milestone 1,000,000th Holden produced, and the prestigious Premier luxury model with standard automatic, leather bucket seats, and metallic paint. In August 1963, the legendary EH debuted Holden's all-new, world-class 'Red Motor' inline-six—featuring a 7-bearing crankshaft, hydraulic lifters, and 149ci (2.4L) and 179ci (2.9L) capacities. The EH became Australia's fastest-selling car ever, selling over 250,000 units in 18 months and claiming podium fame at Mount Panorama with the EH S4 Bathurst homologation special. The 1965 HD brought wider passenger accommodations and the twin-carburettor X2 engine, while the April 1966 HR resolved styling with crisp modern lines, front disc brakes, wider track, and the 186S engine with twin-barrel Bendix-Stromberg WW carburettor.

all_models.name: Camry
all_models.overview: The Toyota Camry was the cornerstone of Australian automotive manufacturing from 1987 to 2017. Built in Port Melbourne and Altona, it was Australia's favourite mid-size family and fleet sedan for over three decades.

all_models.name: Corolla
all_models.overview: The Toyota Corolla is the world's most produced passenger car and an integral part of Australian life. Assembled locally in Victoria for over 30 years (1968-1999), it has provided dependable motoring for generations of Australians.

all_models.name: Pulsar
all_models.overview: The Nissan Pulsar is one of Australia's most historic small-car badges. Manufactured locally at Nissan's Clayton plant in Victoria through the 1980s and early 1990s, the Pulsar sired genuine Australian performance legends, from the local 1980s Pulsar Turbo ET to the iconic N14/N15 Pulsar SSS with its high-revving 2.0-litre SR20DE engine and the rally-homologated N14 GTI-R.

all_models.name: Beetle, Kombi & Country Buggy
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Convertible / Microbus / Van / Ute / Off-Roader
all_models.overview: The bedrock of Volkswagen's Australian history. Starting with CKD assembly in Melbourne in 1954, the Type 1 Beetle and Type 2 Kombi progressed to full local manufacture at Clayton, Victoria, achieving over 80% Australian domestic content. Clayton also designed and manufactured the unique Australian Volkswagen Country Buggy (Type 197).

all_models.name: Golf
all_models.overview: The benchmark European hatchback in Australia across eight generations. The Golf introduced front-wheel drive hatchback dynamics to Australia, initially assembled locally at Clayton, Victoria, and evolved into Australia's favorite hot hatchback through the legendary Golf GTI and all-wheel-drive Golf R.

all_models.name: Chrysler Valiant
all_models.overview: The Chrysler Valiant was the spirited contender of the Australian family car triumvirate alongside the Holden Kingswood and Ford Falcon. Manufactured at Chrysler Australia's sprawling Tonsley Park complex in Adelaide from 1962 to 1981 across 13 series (R, S, AP5, AP6, VC, VE, VF, VG, VH, VJ, VK, CL, CM), the Valiant established an enduring reputation for unmatched horsepower, introducing the 145 hp Slant-6 in 1962, Australia's first family car V8 in 1965, the world-renowned Australian-engineered HEMI-6 in 1970, and pioneering Electronic Lean Burn (ELB) computer management.

all_models.name: Ford Cortina
all_models.overview: The Ford Cortina held a distinguished two-decade tenure in Australia, evolving from a nimble British compact into a uniquely Australian six-cylinder muscle sedan. Assembled locally from 1962 (Mk1 and Mk2), the Cortina achieved legendary status when the Bob Jane / Harry Firth Cortina GT500 won the 1965 Armstrong 500 at Mount Panorama, Bathurst. In 1971, Ford Australia undertook a daring local engineering feat with the TC and TD Cortina: modifying the British 'Coke-bottle' body with an elongated front structure to accommodate Ford Australia's heavy 200ci (3.3L) and 250ci (4.1L) Falcon inline-six engines. The European-styled TE (1977) and TF (1980) brought crisp lines, Ghia luxury, and the sporty X-Pack before being succeeded by the Mazda-based Telstar in 1982.

all_models.name: FPV GT & F6
all_models.overview: The FPV GT and F6 were Ford Performance Vehicles' crowning high-performance icons. Developed in Campbellfield, Victoria by Ford Australia and Prodrive, this duo formed the greatest domestic performance confrontation in Australian history against HSV. The GT revived Ford's iconic muscle heritage with the quad-cam 32-valve Boss 290 and Boss 315 V8s, before adopting the supercharged 5.0L 'Miami' V8 and culminating in the 2014 GT-F 351 (delivering over 400kW on overboost). Concurrently, the F6 Typhoon transformed Australian performance perceptions with its devastating turbocharged Barra 4.0-litre straight-six, producing up to 565Nm of flat-line torque and supercar acceleration.

all_models.name: Holden Cruze
all_models.overview: The Holden Cruze nameplate lived two major chapters in Australia. First launched from 2002 to 2006 as the YG Cruze, it was an innovative subcompact all-wheel-drive crossover co-developed with Suzuki (based on the Ignis) featuring elevated ground clearance and 1.5L power. In 2009, Holden revived the name with the JG Cruze sedan. Most significantly, from March 2011 until October 2016, Holden invested over $1 billion to manufacture the JH Cruze Series II locally on a dedicated assembly line alongside the Commodore at Elizabeth, South Australia. The Australian-built Cruze featured an Australian-designed 5-door hatchback body style, local steering and suspension tuning, high-spec SRi and SRi-V turbo models (1.4L and 1.6L 132 kW turbos), and an efficient 2.0L Turbo Diesel. Over 125,000 Cruzes were built at Elizabeth.

all_models.name: Holden Sandman
all_models.overview: The Holden Sandman is the undisputed emblem of 1970s Australian youth and beach culture. Introduced in January 1974 on the HQ series (option package XX7 / XU3), the Sandman transformed humble commercial panel vans and utilities into vibrant, psychedelic recreational machines. Featuring bold side stripes, Monaro GTS sports dashboard with tachometer, GTS steering wheel, slotted steel rally wheels, twin bucket seats, and standard or optional 253ci and 308ci Red V8 power, the Sandman became a pop-culture legend closely tied to surfing, drive-in cinemas, and Australian freedom. The Sandman package carried through the HQ, HJ, HX, and HZ series until 1980, with authentic surviving examples now among Australia's most fiercely sought-after collector cars.

all_models.name: HSV ClubSport & GTS
all_models.overview: The HSV ClubSport and GTS formed the beating heart of Holden Special Vehicles from 1990 to 2017. Developed at HSV's performance facility in Clayton, Victoria, the ClubSport was HSV's top-selling performance sedan, while the GTS served as the technological flagship. From the original VN ClubSport and VP GTS (with 4-bolt mains and IRS) to the stroker 5.7L V8s, the 300kW Callaway C4B in the VT/VX, the E-Series Magnetic Ride Control, the supercharged 430kW LSA in GEN-F, and the crowning 2017 GTSR W1 (powered by the dry-sump 474kW Corvette ZR1 LS9 supercharged V8), this model line represents the pinnacle of Australian rear-wheel-drive muscle car engineering.

all_models.name: Crown
all_models.overview: The Toyota Crown established Toyota's reputation for engineering refinement and reliability in Australia. Built locally from CKD packs by Australian Motor Industries (AMI) in Port Melbourne from 1967 to 1979, the Crown offered six-cylinder prestige, luxurious appointments, and long-legged durability across five distinct Australian generations.

all_models.name: Corvette & Silverado
all_models.overview: The modern pillars of General Motors in Australia under GM Specialty Vehicles (GMSV). The eighth-generation C8 Corvette arrived as the world's first factory right-hand drive Corvette directly from the Bowling Green assembly line, offering mid-engine supercar performance and the spine-tingling 500kW flat-plane crank Z06. Alongside it, the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and 2500HD are remanufactured to RHD in Melbourne by Walkinshaw Automotive Group, delivering up to 1,322Nm of Duramax V8 torque and heavy towing capability.

all_models.name: Chrysler Centura
all_models.overview: The Chrysler Centura (KB and KC series) was Chrysler Australia's audacious weapon to conquer the mid-size family car market dominated by the Holden Torana and Ford Cortina. Assembled at Tonsley Park in Adelaide, Chrysler imported European Simca 180 bodyshells from France and undertook radical local re-engineering to shoehorn Chrysler Australia's mighty Australian-cast 3.5L (Hemi 215) and 4.0L (Hemi 245) pushrod straight-six engines, alongside a French 2.0L Simca 4-cylinder. With 123 kW (165 hp) and 319 Nm of torque propelling a compact 1,200 kg body, the Hemi 245 Centura was an astonishing sleeper muscle sedan, sprinting from 0-100 km/h in under 9 seconds and completing the standing quarter-mile in 16.5 seconds. 19,770 units were produced across the KB (1975-1977) and updated KC (1977-1978).

all_models.name: Chrysler / Mitsubishi Sigma
all_models.overview: The Chrysler Sigma—later renamed Mitsubishi Sigma after Mitsubishi acquired Chrysler Australia in 1980—was the undisputed king of Australia's four-cylinder family car market across the late 1970s and 1980s. Manufactured at Tonsley Park in Adelaide, the Sigma (GE, GH, GJ, GK, GN) dethroned traditional six-cylinder cars by offering expansive interior space, European-influenced styling, four-wheel coil spring suspension, and revolutionary 'Silent Shaft' counter-rotating balance shafts in its Australian-cast Astron 1.85L, 2.0L, and 2.6L engines. The GH series introduced the legendary limited-edition Sigma Turbo in 1981 (Australia's first locally built turbocharged production car), while the 1982 GJ series spawned the celebrated Peter Wherrett Special. Over 300,000 Sigmas were built in Adelaide before making way for the Magna.

all_models.name: Ford F-Series (F-100 / F-250 / F-350 / F-150)
all_models.overview: The Ford F-Series is an enduring pillar of Australian outback, farming, and heavy towing history. Locally assembled in Australia across multiple decades in Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland, Australian F-100s, F-250s, and F-350s were specifically tailored for harsh Aussie work, utilizing local 250ci Falcon straight-sixes, 300ci big sixes, and Geelong-cast 302ci and 351ci Cleveland V8s. In 2001, Ford Australia officially returned to the heavy-duty market with the mighty RN-series F-250 and F-350, powered by the thunderous 7.3L Navistar Power Stroke Turbo Diesel V8 (175 kW / 684 Nm), creating a cult legend among caravan haulers. In 2023, Ford Australia officially launched the Next-Gen F-150 in Australia, remanufactured to OEM right-hand drive in Mickleham, Victoria featuring the 298 kW 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 and 4.5-tonne towing capacity.

all_models.name: Ford Mustang
all_models.overview: The Ford Mustang has a storied heritage in Australia stretching back six decades. In 1965, Ford Australia officially imported and converted 400 iconic 1965-1966 notchback Mustangs to right-hand drive at Homebush, NSW, while touring car legend Norm Beechey campaigned a 1965 Mustang to Australia's first Australian Touring Car Championship win for an American V8. In 2001, Ford Tickford Experience (FTE) in Campbellfield, Victoria undertook a heroic $4 million engineering program to convert 250 SVT Mustang Cobras featuring independent rear suspension and 240 kW 4.6L DOHC 32V modular V8s. In late 2015, Ford delivered the first global factory right-hand drive FM Mustang to Australia, creating unprecedented multi-year customer waiting lists. The FM/FN generations and all-new 2024+ S650 generation (featuring the 362 kW 5.0L Gen-4 Coyote V8 and 373 kW Dark Horse) made Mustang Australia's best-selling sports car for seven consecutive years.

all_models.name: Ford Territory
all_models.overview: The Ford Territory was the first and only sports utility vehicle (SUV) designed, engineered, and manufactured in Australia. Developed under the code-name 'E265' at a cost of $500 million, the Territory debuted in April 2004 and won the prestigious 2004 Wheels Car of the Year award. Available in 5- and 7-seat configurations, in rear-wheel drive and permanent all-wheel drive, the Territory combined car-like handling, Virtual Pivot Control front suspension, and generous interior packaging, spanning SX, SY, and SZ series with Barra I6, Barra Turbo, and 2.7L V6 turbo-diesel engines.

all_models.name: Holden Adventra & Crewman
all_models.vehicle_type: All-Wheel-Drive Cross Wagon / Dual-Cab Utility / Cab Chassis
all_models.overview: Developed during Holden's multi-million dollar engineering expansion under the VY/VZ Commodore program, the Adventra and Crewman represented audacious Australian engineering innovations. The 2003 Crewman was Australia's first locally designed and manufactured monocoque dual-cab utility, seating five adults on an extended 3,200 mm wheelbase with a heavy-duty leaf-sprung live rear axle capable of carrying up to a tonne. The Adventra was Holden's crossover all-wheel-drive sport wagon, boasting an Australian-engineered 'Cross-Trac' permanent AWD system (62% rear, 38% front torque split with automatic brake-traction management) and raised ground clearance. Holden combined the two concepts to create the monstrous Crewman Cross 8 and Cross 6, alongside V8 SS performance dual-cabs.

all_models.name: Holden FE / FC / FB / EK
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Utility / Panel Van
all_models.overview: The second and third generation post-war Holdens represented major leaps forward in Australian automotive engineering and design. Launched in July 1956, the FE introduced a completely modern, longer, lower body with wrap-around windscreen, 12-volt electrical architecture, recirculating ball steering, and Holden's very first factory station wagon—marketed as the 'Station Sedan'. The May 1958 FC refined the formula with an egg-crate grille and became the first car in Australian history to sell over 100,000 units in a calendar year. In January 1960, the FB adopted American fin-tail styling and a larger 138ci Grey motor, followed in May 1961 by the EK, which brought the historic introduction of the 3-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission to Holden. Across all four series, over 740,000 vehicles were built.

all_models.name: Holden Torana
all_models.overview: The Holden Torana (derived from an Aboriginal word meaning 'to fly') is one of Australian motorsport's greatest legends. Starting in 1967 as a modified Vauxhall Viva four-cylinder compact (HB), the Torana evolved into a giant-killing six-cylinder weapon in the LC and LJ series, highlighted by Peter Brock's rainy 1972 Bathurst 500 victory in the triple-carburettor LJ GTR XU-1. The LH and LX generations made Australian automotive history as the only car platform engineered to accommodate 4-, 6-, and 8-cylinder engines, culminating in the Bathurst-dominating SL/R 5000 and A9X option pack.

all_models.name: Morris Major / Austin Freeway & Wolseley 24/80
all_models.overview: The Morris Major and Austin Freeway family was BMC Australia's dedicated endeavor to engineer vehicles specifically for Australian motoring conditions at the Victoria Park plant in Zetland, Sydney. Commencing in 1958 as the Morris Major (and sibling Austin Lancer), it adapted the Wolseley 1500 body with increased ground clearance, reinforced suspension, and BMC's 1.5L B-Series four. In 1962, BMC Australia achieved an extraordinary domestic engineering feat: by extending the nose structure and casting two extra cylinders onto the 1622cc B-Series block, they created Australia's first locally designed mass-market inline-six: the 2433cc 'Blue Streak' six. Fitted to the Austin Freeway and the luxury Wolseley 24/80 (featuring genuine burr walnut dashboard and leather seats), the 6-cylinder Freeway competed directly with the Holden and Falcon, offering 59 kW, outback suspension, and optional Borg-Warner 35 automatic transmission.

all_models.name: Magna
all_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Magna was an Australian manufacturing triumph, designed specifically for Australian conditions by widening the Japanese Galant by 66mm. Produced at Tonsley Park in Adelaide, it won two Wheels Car of the Year awards (1985, 1996) and culminated in the 180kW Magna Ralliart and revolutionary Magna AWD.

all_models.name: 240 & 850 Series
all_models.overview: The twin legends that transformed Volvo's reputation in Australia. The 240 Series was assembled locally at Clayton, Victoria, setting world safety standards and winning the 1986 Australian Touring Car Championship as the 'Flying Brick'. Its successor, the 850 Series, introduced front-wheel drive transverse 5-cylinder performance, celebrated by the limited-edition 850 T-5R and the 850 Super Tourers raced by Peter Brock and Jim Richards.

all_models.name: Chrysler Valiant Charger
all_models.overview: The Chrysler Valiant Charger is one of the most charismatic muscle cars in Australian history. Launched in August 1971 with the memorable 'Hey Charger!' television advertising campaign, the Charger was built on a shortened 105-inch wheelbase with stunning fastback proportions, winning the 1971 Wheels Car of the Year award. Immortalized by the legendary Bathurst homologation specials—the E38 (280 bhp) and the triple-Weber E49 'Six Pack' (302 bhp)—the Charger was the fastest-accelerating Australian production car for over a decade, holding the standing quarter-mile record at 14.4 seconds.

all_models.name: Dodge Phoenix
all_models.overview: The Dodge Phoenix was Chrysler Australia's grand American luxury flagship from 1960 to 1973. Conceived to compete head-on with the Ford Galaxie and Chevrolet Impala/Bel Air in the prestige government, executive, and pastoralist market, the Phoenix was assembled in Adelaide from North American CKD packs, using Dodge Dart/Polara, Plymouth Fury, and Chrysler bodies married to bespoke factory right-hand drive Plymouth dashboards. Spanning the early finned PD/RD series through to the majestic 'fuselage'-bodied models of 1969-1973, every Phoenix was powered by burly American Chrysler V8 engines—predominantly the 318ci (5.2L) 'Poly' and 'LA' small-block V8s, and the optional 383ci (6.3L) 'B-block' Big Block V8 in the opulent Phoenix 400 Hardtop. Sumptuously appointed with Torqueflite 3-speed automatic transmissions, power steering, push-button radios, and deep plush interiors, the Phoenix was the undisputed car of choice for Australian politicians, judges, and graziers.

all_models.name: Ford Capri
all_models.overview: The Ford Capri represents two bold chapters of Australian automotive innovation. In May 1969, Ford Australia began assembling the sleek Mk1 Capri sports coupe at Homebush, NSW, offering the 1600cc Kent and the potent 3.0-litre 'Essex' V6 in the revered Capri GT 3000 (101 kW / 136 bhp), instantly creating an Australian street and track favorite. In 1989, Ford Australia embarked on Project SA30: designing and manufacturing a dedicated front-wheel-drive 2+2 roadster convertible in Campbellfield, Victoria. Styled by Ghia in Turin and utilizing Mazda 323 mechanicals, the Australian-built Capri (SA, SB, SC, SE) was exported in huge numbers to North America as the Mercury Capri. It produced the blistering turbocharged Capri XR2 and the rare Australian Tickford-tuned Capri Clubsprint Turbo.

all_models.name: Ford Escort
all_models.overview: The Ford Escort was Ford Australia's frontline small car and grassroots rally champion throughout the 1970s. Manufactured at Ford's Homebush plant in Sydney, the Australian Mk1 (1970-1975) featured the classic 'dogbone' front grille, Kent Crossflow engines (1.1L, 1.3L, and 1.6L GT), and the legendary imported Twin Cam and RS1600. In 1975, the Australian Mk2 debuted with a squarer aerodynamic profile. Ford Australia equipped the Mk2 with the lively 1.6L Kent and the potent 2.0L OHC Pinto engine, culminating in the iconic Escort RS2000 featuring a polyurethane droop-snoot front nose, four-spoke alloy wheels, Scheel sports bucket seats, and rally-bred handling.

all_models.name: Ford Laser
all_models.overview: The Ford Laser was one of Australia's most beloved small cars, dominating private sales and motoring awards across the 1980s and 1990s. Born from Ford's global partnership with Mazda (sharing the 323 platform), the Laser was manufactured at Ford's Homebush assembly plant in Sydney with distinct styling penned by Ford Australia's design studio. The Laser spawned the iconic 'TX3' badge—an Australian performance sensation that progressed from the twin-carb KA/KB Sport to the ferocious KC/KE and KF/KH TX3 Turbo 4WD, packing a 1.6L/1.8L turbocharged DOHC engine, full-time four-wheel drive, and digital instruments. Sourcing shifted to Japan in 1994 with the imported KJ, KL, and KQ series before the model was succeeded by the Focus.

all_models.name: Holden Monaro
all_models.overview: The Holden Monaro is Australia's most revered two-door muscle car and grand tourer. Introduced in July 1968 with the HK series, the pillarless hardtop coupe captured national imagination by winning the 1968 Bathurst 500 on debut with Bruce McPhee and Barry Mulholland in a GTS 327, followed by Colin Bond's win in the 1969 HT GTS 350. Resurrected thirty-three years later following a sensational reception as the 'Coupe 22' concept at the 1998 Sydney Motor Show, the modern V2 and VZ Monaro CV8 captivated enthusiasts globally and was exported to North America as the Pontiac GTO and the UK as the Vauxhall Monaro.

all_models.name: Defender
all_models.overview: The immortal off-road master of the Australian bush and Australian Defence Force. Built and adapted locally with unique Australian military specifications (Project Perentie 4x4 and 6x6 with Isuzu 4BD1 3.9L engines), live-axle County 110s, and re-imagined for the 21st century as the ultra-capable, luxury L663 Defender.

all_models.name: Austin 1800 / Utility (Landcrab)
all_models.overview: The Austin 1800 (BMC project ADO17, affectionately nicknamed the 'Landcrab' for its broad track and tenacious roadholding) was manufactured in Australia by BMC and later Leyland Australia at the Victoria Park assembly complex in Zetland, Sydney. Featuring Alec Issigonis's revolutionary transverse engine front-wheel-drive layout, Hydrolastic interconnected fluid suspension, and an astonishingly spacious passenger cabin with 70% of car length devoted to passengers, the 1800 won Wheels Car of the Year in 1965. Australia made two world-exclusive contributions to the model: Australian engineers re-engineered the shell with elevated ground clearance and sump protection for outback endurance (proven by an astonishing 2nd place in the gruelling 1968 London-to-Sydney Marathon); and in 1968, Leyland Australia designed and manufactured the world's only Austin 1800 Utility ('Landcrab Ute'), combining front-wheel drive, a completely flat load bed, and Hydrolastic self-levelling suspension that kept the ute flat regardless of cargo weight! Over 56,000 Austin 1800s were built in Sydney.

all_models.name: Classic Mini / Cooper / Moke
all_models.overview: The full story of the Mini in Australia: manufactured in Sydney at BMC Zetland (with Australian-developed wind-up windows and quarter-vents), immortalized by outright victory in the 1966 Bathurst 500, transformed into the Australian-engineered Californian Moke, and reborn as the modern BMW MINI Cooper and John Cooper Works.

The Mitsubishi 380 was the final passenger car designed, engineered, and manufactured by Mitsubishi Motors Australia at its Tonsley Park plant in Adelaide. Backed by a $600-million investment and over 2.4 million kilometres of Australian testing, the 380 was powered by a punchy 3.8-litre 6G75 V6 with 175kW and 343Nm, praised by critics for its exceptionally stiff body structure and European-grade chassis dynamics.

all_models.name: Skyline
all_models.overview: The Nissan Skyline represents a crowning achievement in Australian motoring. Locally built at Clayton, Victoria in R31 guise with the RB30E engine, it also dominated Bathurst as the twin-turbo R32 GT-R 'Godzilla', ending the V8 monopoly and reshaping Australian motorsport history.

The legendary French workhorses assembled in Melbourne for almost two decades. Revered across Australia for soaking up horrific outback corrugations with long-travel independent suspension, victorious in the 1970 Ampol Trial, and winning 1970 Wheels Car of the Year.

all_models.name: RAM 1500
all_models.overview: The full-size pickup that rewrote the Australian light commercial market. Re-engineered and remanufactured from left-hand drive to right-hand drive by Walkinshaw Automotive in Clayton, Victoria. Delivers 4.5-tonne towing, legendary 5.7L HEMI V8 rumble, expansive crew-cab luxury, and the 523kW supercharged TRX halo.

all_models.name: Aurion
all_models.overview: The Toyota Aurion was an Australian-manufactured large front-wheel-drive sedan engineered to compete directly against the Holden Commodore and Ford Falcon. Powered exclusively by the 200kW 3.5-litre 2GR-FE V6 and built at Altona, Victoria, it also sired the legendary Eaton TVS supercharged 241kW TRD Aurion.

all_models.name: Bolwell Nagari (Mk VIII)
all_models.overview: The Bolwell Nagari (Mk VIII) was Australia's premier bespoke production sports car, built by Campbell and Graeme Bolwell in Mordialloc, Melbourne. Featuring an ultra-rigid Y-shaped steel backbone chassis, breathtaking fiberglass coachwork, and Ford 302ci/351ci Windsor and Cleveland V8 engines, the Nagari weighed just 1,040 kg and accelerated from 0-100 km/h in 5.8 seconds, outpacing contemporary European exotics. A total of 127 units (100 coupes and 27 convertibles) were built.

all_models.name: Ford Fairlane & LTD
all_models.overview: The Ford Fairlane and LTD was Australia's definitive long-wheelbase luxury prestige sedan. Spanning four decades and eleven model series from the 1967 ZA to the 2007 BF Mk II, the Fairlane dominated Australian corporate, hire-car, and government limousine fleets. In 1973, Ford introduced the ultra-exclusive LTD (P5) riding on a limousine-class 121-inch wheelbase with concealed headlamps and standard 351 Cleveland V8. The Fairlane and LTD offered effortless V8 cruising, cavernous rear legroom, and refined Australian engineering.

all_models.name: Goggomobil Dart
all_models.overview: The Goggomobil Dart is Australia's most famous and beloved micro-sports car. Conceived and designed by Sydney automotive pioneer Bill Buckle to bypass steep tariffs on imported fully assembled cars, the Dart combined German Hans Glas rolling chassis components with an ultra-lightweight, doorless aerodynamic fiberglass roadster body molded in Brookvale, Sydney. Standing just 1.1 meters tall and weighing only 345 kg, the Dart became an Australian cultural icon, celebrated for its playful styling and immortalized in Australian television advertisements.

all_models.name: Holden Statesman / Caprice
all_models.overview: The Holden Statesman and Caprice was Australia's presidential luxury flagship for nearly five decades. Conceived to challenge the Ford Fairlane and LTD, the Statesman rode on an extended 114-inch to 118-inch wheelbase providing unmatched rear legroom. Serving as official transport for Australian prime ministers, diplomats, business executives, and luxury hire car fleets, the Statesman and Caprice evolved from the ornate HQ-WB models to the modern IRS-equipped VQ-WL series and the billion-dollar Zeta-platform WM and WN. Exported globally as the Chevrolet Caprice, Buick Park Avenue, and US Police Pursuit Vehicle (PPV).

all_models.name: Leyland P76
all_models.overview: The Leyland P76 was Australia's most daring automotive gamble. Developed under project leader Peter North at BMC/Leyland's Zetland plant in Sydney to break the Holden-Ford-Chrysler monopoly, the P76 was styled by Italian master Giovanni Michelotti. It boasted world-class engineering: an all-aluminium 4.4-litre V8 derived from Rover weighing less than rivals' iron sixes, standard front power disc brakes, MacPherson strut front suspension, side-impact door bars, and a boot famously demonstrated by swallowing an entire 44-gallon drum. The P76 won the 1973 Wheels Car of the Year and conquered the 1974 World Cup Rally across the Sahara before factory closure cut short its life.

all_models.name: Brabham BT62 / BT62R
all_models.overview: The Brabham BT62 and BT62R was an ultra-exclusive mid-engine hypercar manufactured in Adelaide, South Australia by Brabham Automotive, led by Le Mans winner David Brabham. Developed without turbochargers or hybrid battery weight, the BT62 featured a high-tensile tubular steel chassis with integrated carbon-kevlar monocoque safety cell, carbon-fibre body panels, and a mid-mounted naturally aspirated 5.4-litre modular V8 revving to 8,200 rpm and developing 522 kW (700 hp) and 667 Nm. Generating 1,200 kg of aerodynamic downforce with a dry weight of only 972 kg, the BT62 shattered closed-cockpit lap records at Mount Panorama Bathurst (1m 58.69s).

all_models.name: Giocattolo Group B
all_models.overview: The Giocattolo Group B was an authentic Australian mid-engine supercar engineered by entrepreneur Paul Halstead and former McLaren Formula One designer Barry Lock in Caloundra, Queensland. Starting with imported Alfa Romeo Sprint bodyshells, Halstead and Lock discarded the front-drive powertrain and installed a mid-mounted Walkinshaw-fettled Holden Special Vehicles 5.0L Group A V8 (220kW/300hp), a bespoke ZF 5DS-25/2 five-speed transaxle, Kevlar/carbon-fibre composite bodywork, and Brembo racing brakes. Accelerating from 0-100 km/h in 4.5 seconds with a top speed of 260 km/h, only 15 production cars were built before funding ended in 1989.

all_models.name: HDT VK SS Group A ('Blue Meanie')
all_models.overview: The HDT VK SS Group A, universally affectionately known as the 'Blue Meanie', is the most revered homologation muscle car in Australian touring car racing history. Built by Peter Brock's Holden Dealer Team Special Vehicles at 124 Bertie Street, Port Melbourne in 1985, the Group A was created to homologate the Commodore under international FIA Group A racing regulations. All 500 cars were painted in striking Formula Blue, featuring a de-stroked 4.9-litre (4987cc) V8 with Crane cam and roller rockers, M21 4-speed manual gearbox, Scheel velour bucket seats, and distinctive white 16-inch Aero alloy wheels.

all_models.name: Holden 48-215 (FX)
all_models.overview: The Holden 48-215 (retrospectively referred to as the 'FX') was Australia's first mass-produced domestic motor vehicle, famously unveiled on 29 November 1948 by Prime Minister Ben Chifley with the words: 'She's a beauty!'. Developed under GM Project 2000, it combined American interior room and robust unibody construction with European operating economy, tailored specifically for Australia's harsh corrugated roads. In January 1951, the 50-2106 Coupe Utility was launched, defining the iconic Australian 'ute', followed in July 1953 by the 48-215-257 Business Sedan for taxi operators. Over 120,402 examples were produced.

all_models.name: Holden FJ
all_models.overview: Launched in October 1953, the Holden FJ is Australia's most recognized cultural automotive icon of the 1950s. Featuring an assertive horizontal chrome tooth grille, redesigned torpedo rear styling, and the introduction of the luxurious 'Special' sedan badge with two-tone leather options, the FJ captured 50% of Australian new car registrations. In December 1953, the iconic FJ Panel Van was introduced, creating the quintessential Aussie tradesman vehicle. The FJ was also Holden's first exported model, shipped to New Zealand in 1954. Total production reached 169,969 units.

all_models.name: Holden Gemini
all_models.overview: The Holden Gemini was Australia's best-selling four-cylinder car of the 1970s and early 1980s. Developed from GM's global T-car platform (shared with the Opel Kadett C, Isuzu Bellett Gemini, and Chevrolet Chevette), the Gemini won the prestigious 1975 Wheels Car of the Year award on debut. Over 226,000 units were produced across TX, TC, TD, TE, TF, and TG rear-wheel-drive series before transitioning to the front-wheel-drive RB series.

all_models.name: Lightburn Zeta Sedan
all_models.overview: The Lightburn Zeta was South Australia's unique fiberglass microcar, manufactured by industrial equipment firm Lightburn & Co. in Camden Park, Adelaide. Powered by a British Villiers 324cc two-stroke twin-cylinder motorcycle engine driving the front wheels through a 4-speed sequential dog transaxle without reverse (the engine was stopped and restarted in reverse rotation), the Zeta was impervious to corrosion and designed to provide economical suburban motoring.

all_models.name: OKA 4x4 (LT, XT, NT)
all_models.overview: The OKA 4x4 was an uncompromising, severe-duty all-terrain four-wheel-drive commercial truck manufactured in Bibra Lake, Perth, Western Australia. Engineered specifically to endure the most punishing outback corrugations, mine sites, and desert terrain across Australia, the OKA featured an indestructible heavy-duty perimeter box-section chassis, Dana 60 front and Dana 70 rear live drive axles, New Process transfer case, and Perkins/Cummins turbo-diesel power across LT, XT, and NT generations.

all_models.name: Morris Minor
all_models.overview: Sir Alec Issigonis' masterpiece, assembled in Sydney in huge numbers with local body pressings and beloved by generations of Australians.

all_models.name: Austin 1800 (Landcrab & Ute)
all_models.overview: Vast interior space and Hydrolastic suspension, adapted with heavy-duty Australian dust sealing and transformed into the Aussie Austin 1800 ute.

all_models.name: Morris Kimberley / Tasman (BMC X6)
all_models.overview: Australian-designed and built family car featuring the world's first transverse-mounted overhead-cam six-cylinder engine (2.2L E6).

all_models.name: Bolwell Mk IV
all_models.overview: The earliest commercial Bolwell sports car, offered as a fiberglass body-chassis unit accepting Ford Ten or Cortina running gear.

all_models.name: Bolwell Mk VII
all_models.overview: Sleek fastback sports coupe based on Holden mechanicals (186 Red motor), setting the stage for the Nagari.

all_models.name: Bolwell Ikara
all_models.overview: Radical mid-engine open sports car utilizing a spaceframe chassis and Volkswagen Golf mechanicals.

all_models.name: Bolwell Nagari 300 / 500
all_models.overview: 21st-century Australian carbon-composite supercar featuring mid-mounted 3.5L V6 or 375kW 6.2L Chevrolet LS3 V8.

all_models.name: Silverado 1500
all_models.overview: Full-size pickup remanufactured by Walkinshaw at Clayton VIC, powered by a 6.2-litre EcoTec3 V8 with 10-speed automatic and 4.5-tonne towing.

all_models.name: Chrysler Royal
all_models.overview: Locally developed luxury flagship combining 1954 Plymouth body pressings with sweeping tail fins, dual headlamps, and push-button automatic transmission across AP1, AP2, and AP3 series.

all_models.name: Chrysler Valiant Utility
all_models.overview: Chrysler Australia's rugged coupe utility (Wayfarer and Valiant Utility) matching Holden and Falcon utes with superior Slant-6 and Hemi-6 hauling power.

all_models.name: Chrysler Galant
all_models.overview: First collaboration between Chrysler Australia and Mitsubishi Motors, assembled at Tonsley Park with Saturn and Astron 4-cylinder engines.

all_models.name: DS / ID
all_models.overview: The Goddess of automotive design, assembled in Victoria and celebrated for conquering the brutal Ampol Trial with hydropneumatic suspension.

all_models.name: Phoenix
all_models.overview: Assembled at Chrysler Australia's Tonsley Park plant in South Australia, offering full-size luxury, V8 power, and flamboyant American styling.

all_models.name: 500 / Bambino
all_models.overview: Beloved Italian design icon, assembled locally as the classic Bambino and reborn as the chic modern 500, Abarth, and electric 500e.

all_models.name: Ford Model T
all_models.overview: The car that put Australia on wheels. Locally assembled in Geelong from Canadian knock-down kits starting in 1925, featuring rugged high ground clearance for outback tracks.

all_models.name: Ford Model A
all_models.overview: Successor to the Model T, offering modern controls, safety glass, standard four-wheel mechanical brakes, and handsome styling.

all_models.name: Ford V8 (Model 18 / Custom / De Luxe)
all_models.overview: Pioneered mass-market V8 motoring in Australia with the Flathead V8, and birthed the world's first coupe utility in Geelong in 1934.

all_models.name: Ford Prefect
all_models.overview: British Ford small family car assembled in Australia across E93A, E493A, and 100E generations, including local coupe utility variants.

all_models.name: Ford Anglia
all_models.overview: Popular British-designed small car assembled in Australia, concluding with the iconic reverse-rake rear window 105E.

all_models.name: Ford Consul
all_models.overview: Modern unibody sedan with MacPherson strut front suspension, assembled in Australia with unique local ute variants.

all_models.name: Ford Zephyr
all_models.overview: Six-cylinder flagship of British Ford, manufactured with high local content in Geelong and Broadmeadows before being superseded by the Falcon.

all_models.name: Ford Zodiac
all_models.overview: Upmarket luxury variant of the Zephyr featuring two-tone paint, leather seating, whitewall tyres, and twin carburettors.

all_models.name: Ford Falcon Utility & Panel Van
all_models.vehicle_type: Coupe Utility / Panel Van / Cab Chassis
all_models.overview: The definitive Australian workhorse and recreational vehicle, offering unmatched durability, leaf-spring load-carrying capability, and legendary XR6 Turbo and XR8 performance trims.

all_models.name: Ford Landau
all_models.overview: Exclusive two-door personal luxury coupe combining the Falcon Hardtop body with the opulent front clip of the P5 LTD, featuring pop-up headlight shutters and standard 351 Cleveland V8.

all_models.name: Ford Meteor
all_models.overview: The sedan and wagon sibling to the Laser hatchback, assembled at Homebush, NSW with upscale frontal styling and plush trim.

all_models.name: Ford Telstar
all_models.overview: Highly successful mid-size car built in Australia (AR-AT) and later imported from Japan (AV-AY), sharing engineering with the Mazda 626.

all_models.name: Ford Corsair
all_models.overview: Badge-engineered Nissan Pintara built under the Button Car Plan at Nissan's Clayton, Victoria plant.

all_models.name: Ford Transit
all_models.overview: The global gold standard of commercial vans. Assembled locally at Homebush and Broadmeadows with local Falcon sixes before transitioning to European imports and Transit Custom.

all_models.name: FPV Pursuit & Super Pursuit
all_models.overview: FPV's high-performance utes packing Boss V8, supercharged Miami V8, and F6 Tornado turbo six firepower.

all_models.name: FPV F6X
all_models.overview: Australia's fastest SUV at launch. Engineered from the Ford Territory with the 270kW Barra Turbo six, full-time AWD, and Brembo six-piston brakes.

all_models.name: FPV GS
all_models.overview: Accessible FPV entry point introduced in 2009 with Boss 302 V8 and upgraded in 2010 to a 302kW version of the supercharged Miami 5.0L V8.

all_models.name: Buckle Goggomobil Sedan / Coupe / Van
all_models.overview: Locally molded fiberglass-bodied Goggomobil microcars produced in Sydney, including the Regent sedan, TS coupe, and Transporter van.

all_models.name: HDT VC Brock Commodore
all_models.overview: The original Brock road car. 500 individually numbered cars in Firethorn Red, Palais White, and Tuxedo Black with 160kW 5.0L V8 and Irmscher alloys.

all_models.name: HDT VH SS Group 1, 2 & 3
all_models.overview: The car that defined 1980s Australian street performance, culminating in the Group 3 with Brock's modified 180kW blueprint 5.0L V8.

all_models.name: HDT VL SS Group A & Director
all_models.overview: The final factory-supported Brock Commodores (VL Group A in Permanent Red) and the infamous, opulent Director that triggered the split with Holden.

all_models.name: HDT Magnum
all_models.overview: HDT's luxurious grand-touring adaptation of the WB Statesman de Ville and WB utility, featuring Group 3 V8 power and high-speed touring stability.

all_models.name: HDT Monza
all_models.overview: Peter Brock's concept to produce a European grand tourer in Australia, transplanting Holden 5.0L V8s and Supra 5-speed gearboxes into Opel Monza fastback coupes.

all_models.name: HDT Heritage & Retro Series
all_models.overview: Modern bespoke tribute vehicles built on VE and VF Commodore platforms recreating iconic VC, VH, and VK Blue Meanie designs with 6.0L/6.2L V8 power.

all_models.name: Hillman Hunter / Arrow
all_models.overview: Assembled at Port Melbourne VIC, celebrated for winning the grueling 1968 London to Sydney Marathon.

all_models.name: Hillman Minx
all_models.overview: One of Australia's most ubiquitous post-war family cars, assembled in Melbourne with local coupe utility derivatives.

all_models.name: Holden FE
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: First major redesign with contemporary low-line styling, curved one-piece windscreen, 12-volt electrical system, and the introduction of the first Holden Station Sedan (wagon).

all_models.name: Holden FC
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: Facelifted FE featuring bolder grille, tail-fin chrome spears, upgraded interior, and improved 72 bhp Grey engine. Captured over 50% of the Australian passenger vehicle market.

all_models.name: Holden FB
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: American-inspired styling with wraparound dogleg windscreen, rear finettes, and increased interior room. The first Holden exported in left-hand drive.

all_models.name: Holden EK
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: The first Holden to offer an automatic transmission—the 3-speed GM Hydra-Matic imported from the United States. Also introduced electric windscreen wipers.

all_models.name: Holden EJ
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: Clean modern European-influenced styling that shed fins and wraparound glass. Introduced the ultra-luxurious Premier badge with leather upholstery and standard Hydra-Matic.

all_models.name: Holden EH
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: One of the most beloved Holdens in history, introducing the revolutionary overhead-valve 'Red' six-cylinder engines (149ci and 179ci) with seven-bearing crankshafts.

all_models.name: Holden HD
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: Wider, longer body featuring distinctive kidney-grille front styling and sharp front fender extensions. Introduced the twin-carburettor X2 high-performance engine option.

all_models.name: Holden HR
all_models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
all_models.overview: Clever restyle of the HD with smoothed front fenders and vertical tail lamps. Introduced enlarged 161ci and 186ci Red engines, wider wheel track, and standard seatbelt anchorages.

all_models.name: Holden Camira
all_models.overview: Holden's version of GM's global J-Car platform, winning 1982 Wheels Car of the Year for its ride and packaging before being challenged by early quality control issues.

all_models.name: Holden Adventra
all_models.overview: Cross-over all-wheel-drive wagon based on the VY II/VZ Commodore wagon with Cross Trac permanent AWD (62% rear torque bias) and raised ride height.

all_models.name: Holden Crewman
all_models.overview: Australian-designed and built 4-door dual-cab ute built on the extended long-wheelbase Statesman chassis, offered in RWD and Cross Trac AWD (Cross 6 / Cross 8).

all_models.name: Holden Vectra
all_models.overview: European-designed mid-size car imported initially from Belgium then manufactured locally at Elizabeth SA (1998-2001) before reverting to German imports (ZC).

all_models.name: Holden Nova
all_models.overview: Badge-engineered Toyota Corolla built alongside the Corolla under the UAAI joint venture at Altona and Dandenong, Victoria.

all_models.name: Holden Apollo
all_models.overview: Badge-engineered Toyota Camry built in Victoria under the UAAI joint venture, offering outstanding reliability with Holden branding.

all_models.name: Holden Sunbird
all_models.overview: The 4-cylinder iteration of the Torana body, re-engineered as an economy family car following fuel price shocks.

all_models.name: Holden Brougham
all_models.overview: Holden's first bespoke luxury vehicle, built on the HK/HT/HG Premier body with an extended 8-inch rear overhang to challenge the Ford Fairlane.

all_models.name: HSV VL SS Group A SV
all_models.overview: The foundational car of HSV. A wild wind-tunnel-developed Group A homologation special finished in Panorama Silver with twin-throttle 5.0L V8.

all_models.name: HSV Senator
all_models.overview: HSV's executive express, combining luxury appointments, premium leather, discreet aerodynamic styling, and potent V8 powertrains.

all_models.name: HSV Maloo
all_models.overview: The world's fastest production utility. Named from the Indigenous Australian word for 'thunder', the Maloo set Guinness World Records for ute speed.

all_models.name: HSV Grange
all_models.overview: Flagship performance limousine built on the long-wheelbase Statesman and Caprice bodies, named after Penfolds Grange Hermitage.

all_models.name: HSV Coupe GTO & Coupe GTS
all_models.overview: Sensational performance coupes crafted on the third-generation Holden Monaro body, featuring aggressive styling and up to 300kW Callaway C4B power.

all_models.name: HSV Avalanche & Avalanche XUV
all_models.overview: High-performance all-wheel-drive crossover wagon and XUV dual-cab utility based on the Adventra/Crewman platform with Cross Trac AWD and 5.7L LS1 V8.

all_models.name: HSV W427
all_models.overview: HSV's 20th anniversary masterpiece. Hand-assembled at Clayton with the Corvette Z06's dry-sump 7.0-litre (427ci) LS7 V8, producing 375kW and 640Nm.

all_models.name: HSV Colorado SportsCat
all_models.overview: Re-engineered Holden Colorado dual-cab 4WD featuring MTV dampers or Supashock suspension, Cooper Zeon tyres, and AP Racing 4-piston brakes.

all_models.name: Morris Minor
all_models.overview: Alec Issigonis's brilliant small car, assembled at Zetland with high local content in sedan, convertible, commercial van, and uniquely Australian coupe utility forms.

all_models.name: Morris Major
all_models.overview: Australian-unique compact car developed by BMC Australia at Zetland from the Wolseley 1500, tailored with heavy-duty suspension for Australian country roads.

all_models.name: Austin Lancer
all_models.overview: The Austin-badged twin of the Morris Major featuring a traditional Austin chrome crinkle grille and horseshoe motif.

all_models.name: Austin Freeway
all_models.overview: BMC Australia's contender against the Holden EJ and Falcon XK, created by stretching the Cambridge body and fitting the local 2.4L 'Blue Streak' inline-six.

all_models.name: Morris / BMC Mini
all_models.overview: The revolutionary front-wheel-drive transverse marvel, built at Zetland with Australian-developed innovations including wind-up windows, Mini K, and Cooper S (1966 Bathurst 1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8-9 finish).

all_models.name: Morris / Leyland Mini Moke
all_models.overview: The cheerful open-air doorless beach utility. When UK production ended in 1968, Australia became the worldwide manufacturing home, creating the 13-inch wheel Californian.

all_models.name: Morris 1100 / 1500 / Nomad
all_models.overview: Advanced Pininfarina-styled front-wheel-drive family car featuring Hydrolastic interconnected fluid suspension, culminating in the Australian-exclusive 1500 OHC engine and 5-door Nomad hatchback.

all_models.name: Austin Kimberley & Tasman (X6)
all_models.overview: Australian-styled evolution of the 1800 platform (Project X6) powered by an Australian-developed transverse 2.2L E-Series overhead-cam six-cylinder engine.

all_models.name: Leyland Marina
all_models.overview: Rear-wheel-drive compact car built at Zetland, uniquely adapted for Australia with the 2.6L OHC E-series six-cylinder ('Marina Red Six').

all_models.name: Leyland Force 7
all_models.overview: Sensational 2-door hatchback coupe variant of the P76 with full rear tailgate and 4.4L V8. Almost all were crushed when Zetland closed, making surviving cars among the rarest Australian collector vehicles.

all_models.name: Lightburn Zeta Sports
all_models.overview: Rare and charming fiberglass roadster with FMR/Sachs 498cc twin-cylinder engine and Frisky-inspired body lines; only 28 produced.

all_models.name: Lightburn Zeta Utility
all_models.overview: Open-tray micro utility variant of the Zeta built for local councils and light delivery duties.

all_models.name: Classic MGB (Australian Assembled)
all_models.overview: Over 9,000 MGB roadsters assembled locally at Pressed Metal Corp and BMC Zetland Sydney, etching MG into Australian sports car lore.

all_models.name: Sigma
all_models.overview: The car that transformed Tonsley Park; originally sold under Chrysler, then Mitsubishi from 1980.

all_models.name: Verada
all_models.overview: Tonsley Park-built luxury derivative of the Magna, featuring extended equipment, V6 power, and exported as the Diamante.

all_models.name: Colt
all_models.overview: Compact city car, built at Tonsley Park in the 1980s and re-introduced in the 2000s including the Colt Ralliart Turbo.

all_models.name: Laurentian / Parisienne
all_models.overview: Assembled by General Motors-Holden at Fishermans Bend and Elizabeth, representing the height of GM prestige in Australia.

all_models.name: GTO / G8 (Australian Exports)
all_models.overview: Holden's export triumphs: Elizabeth-built Monaro and VE Commodore rebadged as Pontiac muscle icons for the North American market.

all_models.name: RAM 2500 / 3500 Heavy Duty
all_models.overview: Commercial-grade haulers remanufactured at Clayton VIC, powered by the 6.7-litre Cummins inline-six turbo diesel with up to 8-tonne towing ratings.

all_models.name: Rebel / Matador
all_models.overview: Assembled at AMI Port Melbourne, offering smooth American V8 luxury and robust towing capability for Australian conditions.

all_models.name: Javelin
all_models.overview: Ultra-rare Australian muscle car assembled at Port Melbourne from CKD packs, featuring bulging wheel arches and high-output AMC V8s.

all_models.name: 12 / Virage
all_models.overview: Assembled at Heidelberg VIC; acclaimed for ride comfort and ruggedness, culminating in the unique Australian-styled Virage.

all_models.name: SD1 (3500 / 2600)
all_models.overview: Ferrari Daytona-inspired five-door aerodynamic hatchback, powered by the Rover all-alloy 3.5-litre V8 and 1977 Wheels Car of the Year winner.

all_models.name: Lark / Cruiser
all_models.overview: Locally assembled in Sydney and Melbourne; legendary as Australia's premier high-speed police pursuit special of the 1960s.

all_models.name: Tiara
all_models.overview: The first Toyota assembled in Australia by AMI in Port Melbourne, laying the foundation for Toyota's domestic manufacturing history.

all_models.name: Corona
all_models.overview: Long-running Australian family car assembled in Port Melbourne across multiple generations until succeeded by the Camry.

all_models.name: Avalon
all_models.overview: Spacious family and taxi sedan built at Altona to take on Holden Commodore and Ford Falcon.

all_models.name: Lexcen
all_models.overview: Holden Commodore rebadged as a Toyota under the Button Plan joint venture (UAAI), built at Holden's Elizabeth plant.

all_models.name: 2000 / 2500 / 2.5 PI
all_models.overview: Michelotti-designed executive saloon assembled at Port Melbourne VIC, offering independent rear suspension and Lucas mechanical fuel injection.

all_models.name: Velox / Cresta
all_models.overview: Six-cylinder British-designed family cars with unique Australian Holden-built body variants, including the famous Vagabond tourer and coupe utility.

all_models.name: Viva (HA & HB)
all_models.overview: The compact four-cylinder car that directly gave birth to the Holden Torana when adapted for Australian conditions by GM-H.

all_models.name: Beetle
all_models.overview: The car that founded Volkswagen in Australia, built with high local content at Clayton VIC before evolving into the retro New Beetle and Beetle A5.

all_models.name: Kombi / Transporter
all_models.overview: Australia's iconic surf-wagon, delivery van, and camper, assembled at Clayton VIC across T1 and T2 eras, and imported through modern T6.1, T7, and ID.Buzz.

all_models.name: Passat
all_models.overview: Volkswagen's flagship executive sedan and wagon, originally assembled at Clayton and later imported across B1 through B8 generations and Alltrack rugged wagons.

all_models.name: 240 / 260 Series
all_models.overview: Indestructible Swedish family icon assembled locally in Melbourne and Brisbane, celebrated for world-class crashworthiness and 1986 ATCC victory.

all_models.name: Z-Car (Fairlady Z)
all_models.overview: The Datsun and Nissan Z-Car is one of the most celebrated sports car dynasties in Australian automotive history. From the breathtaking 1970 Datsun 240Z that conquered Jaguar E-Types and MGs on price and performance to the twin-turbo technology tour-de-force 300ZX, the pure rear-drive naturally aspirated 350Z and 370Z, and the modern 298kW twin-turbo RZ34 Z Coupe, the Z represents affordable, exhilarating grand touring sports car excellence.

all_models.name: Liberty & Outback
all_models.overview: The Subaru Liberty (Legacy globally) and Outback revolutionized Australian family and touring motoring. Spanning seven generations, the Liberty delivered rally-bred AWD performance with the BC RS Turbo, twin-turbo B4, and 2003 Wheels Car of the Year winning BL/BP GT Spec.B, while the lifted Outback pioneered the crossover wagon genre in 1996 and evolved into Australia's ultimate all-road adventure tourer.

all_models.name: Celica
all_models.overview: The Toyota Celica was Australia's definitive Japanese sports coupe for 34 years across seven generations. From the Mustang-inspired TA22 and RA28 liftbacks of the 1970s to the championship-winning turbo all-wheel-drive GT-Four rally homologation specials and high-revving 2ZZ-GE VVTL-i ZR, the Celica defined stylish sports performance.

all_models.name: LandCruiser
all_models.overview: The LandCruiser is the undisputed King of the Australian Outback. First brought to Australia in 1958 for the Snowy Mountains Scheme, it has conquered the country's most unforgiving deserts, pastoral stations, and mines for nearly seven decades.

all_models.name: 626 / Mazda6
all_models.overview: The Mazda 626 and its successor the Mazda6 served as Australia's benchmark mid-size Japanese passenger car for 45 years. From the 1983 Wheels Car of the Year winning front-wheel drive 626 GC to the ferocious 190kW Mazda6 MPS turbocharged all-wheel-drive performance hero, it balanced executive styling with dynamic driver engagement.

all_models.name: Forester
all_models.overview: The Subaru Forester is an Australian automotive legend that helped pioneer the compact all-wheel-drive crossover genre in 1997. Blending permanent Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive, high ground clearance, commanding estate-car visibility, and turbocharged WRX engines in GT and XT badges, it earned an intensely loyal following among Australian families, campers, and rural motorists.

all_models.name: HiLux
all_models.overview: The Toyota HiLux is an Australian cultural icon and the country's best-selling vehicle outright from 2016 through 2022. Renowned for near-indestructible durability, it serves on construction sites, farms, mining operations, and outback tracks nationwide.

all_models.name: Civic & Civic Type R
all_models.overview: The Honda Civic is an undisputed benchmark of global and Australian automotive engineering. Spanning eleven generations over more than 50 years, the Civic conquered Australian hearts during the 1970s oil crisis with its revolutionary CVCC clean-burn engine, democratized Formula 1-derived VTEC variable valve timing in the 1990s VTi-R, and evolved into front-wheel-drive circuit royalty with the ferocious Civic Type R.

all_models.name: HiAce
all_models.overview: The Toyota HiAce is the unquestioned titan of Australian commercial vans and passenger shuttle transport. Across more than half a century, its cab-over and semi-bonnet configurations have kept Australian tradespeople, couriers, airport shuttles, and tourism fleets moving with renowned reliability and outstanding resale value.

all_models.name: LandCruiser Prado
all_models.overview: The Toyota LandCruiser Prado is Australia's perennial favorite family and long-distance outback touring 4WD. Bridging the gap between the mid-size RAV4 and heavy-duty LandCruiser wagon, the Prado delivers genuine off-road capability, dual long-range fuel tanks, up to seven seats, and legendary durability.

all_models.name: A3, S3 & RS3
all_models.overview: The pioneer of the premium compact segment in Australia. Spanning four generations (8L, 8P, 8V, and 8Y), the A3 introduced luxury hatchback packaging and quattro all-wheel drive, reaching high-performance zeniths with the S3 quattro and the spine-tingling 2.5-litre turbocharged inline-5 Audi RS3 producing 294kW.

all_models.name: 5 Series & M5
all_models.overview: The definitive executive express in Australia across eight generations. The 5 Series established BMW's benchmark rear-wheel-drive chassis dynamics, silky inline-sixes, and thunderous V8s, culminating in the peerless BMW M5 from the high-revving S38, naturally aspirated V8 S62, screaming V10 S85, to the twin-turbo V8 M xDrive M5 Competition.

all_models.name: Mazda3
all_models.overview: The Mazda3 is one of Australia's most beloved passenger cars, achieving the rare feat of becoming the country's outright best-selling vehicle in 2011 and 2012. Known for sporty dynamics, sharp KODO design, and high-performance MPS editions.

all_models.name: MX-5
all_models.overview: The Mazda MX-5 is the world's best-selling two-seater sports car and an icon of pure driving pleasure in Australia. Embodying the philosophy of 'Jinba Ittai' (horse and rider as one), the MX-5 revived the classic British roadster concept with Japanese reliability, near-perfect 50:50 weight distribution, and rear-wheel-drive purity.

all_models.name: E-Class
all_models.overview: The heartbeat of Mercedes-Benz in Australia. From the virtually indestructible W114/W115 and W123 that conquered outback roads and taxi fleets, through the peerless Bruno Sacco W124, to supercharged V8 E55 AMG and twin-turbo 450kW E63 S AMG monsters.

all_models.name: Outlander
all_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Outlander is one of Australia's most enduring family SUVs and a pioneer of plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) technology. Known for offering 7-seat practicality in a medium SUV footprint, robust all-wheel drive systems derived from the Lancer Evolution, and exceptional value, the Outlander is a mainstay on Australian roads.

all_models.name: Navara
