all_models.overview: The Nissan Navara is one of Australia's premier dual-cab and commercial utes. Spanning four generations, from the durable D21 and indestructible D22 workhorses to the powerhouse 550Nm V6 turbodiesel D40 and coil-sprung D23 with locally engineered Premcar Warrior editions, the Navara has served on Australian building sites, farms, and off-road expeditions for nearly four decades.

all_models.name: Patrol
all_models.overview: The Nissan Patrol is an Australian outback giant. In 1962, the G60 Patrol made history as the first motor vehicle to cross the Simpson Desert. Across MQ, GQ, GU, and the V8-powered Y62, it has matched the LandCruiser blow for blow across Australia's harshest terrain.

The definitive rear-engine sports car. Australia boasts one of the most historic ties to Porsche in the world: Melbourne businessman Norman Hamilton secured the Australian concession in 1951, importing two 356s that represented the first right-hand drive Porsches ever made. Since the 911's local launch in 1965, it has defined sports car perfection through air-cooled and water-cooled eras, culminating in legendary Turbo, GT3, and GT3 RS icons.

all_models.name: 3 Series
all_models.overview: The benchmark executive sports sedan in Australia across seven distinct generations: E21, E30, E36, E46, E90, F30, and G20. Revered for near-perfect 50:50 weight distribution, rear-wheel drive chassis balance, silky inline-six engines, and iconic M3 motorsport heroes.

all_models.name: X5
all_models.overview: The vehicle that redefined the luxury SUV category in Australia. Originating in 2000 as the world's first true Sports Activity Vehicle (SAV) with monocoque construction and car-like handling, the BMW X5 has dominated Australian luxury SUV sales across four generations.

all_models.name: Holden Rodeo
all_models.vehicle_type: Ute / Cab Chassis / Space Cab / Crew Cab 4x2 & 4x4
all_models.overview: For nearly three decades from 1980 to 2008, the Holden Rodeo was one of Australia's most trusted commercial workhorses and outback touring utilities. Engineered by Isuzu Motors and sold through Holden dealerships across Australia, the Rodeo spanned the tough KB series (1980-1988), the long-running TF series (1988-2003, famous for its bulletproof 2.8L 4JB1-T turbo-diesel and 3.2L V6), and the redesigned RA series (2003-2008). The Rodeo pioneered crew-cab four-wheel-drive dual-cab versatility in Australia, proving equally adept on cattle stations, mining sites, and suburban driveways before being renamed Colorado in 2008.

all_models.name: X-Trail
all_models.overview: The Nissan X-Trail is an Australian compact and medium SUV institution. Famous for combining utilitarian practicality—such as wipe-clean waterproof cargo floors, cooled cup holders, and multi-tier drawers—with genuine soft-road capability via Nissan's All-Mode 4x4, it remains one of Australia's most consistently popular family crossovers.

all_models.name: WRX
all_models.overview: The Subaru Impreza WRX and WRX STI democratized supercar-baiting all-wheel-drive turbocharged performance in Australia in 1994. Backed by Possum Bourne's seven consecutive Australian Rally Championships, the WRX is an indelible part of modern Australian car culture.

all_models.name: Supra
all_models.overview: The Toyota Supra is a halo sports grand tourer with an indelible legacy in Australian motorsport and enthusiast culture. From early Celica Supra models through the twin-turbo 2JZ-GTE JZA80 supercar killer to the modern B58-powered GR Supra, it represents Toyota's front-engine rear-drive inline-six performance pinnacle.

all_models.name: Echo / Yaris / GR Yaris
all_models.overview: Toyota's light car family in Australia spans from the quirky, spacious Echo through three generations of Yaris hatchbacks and sedans to the hyper-capable GR Yaris Rallye AWD homologation special. Combining exceptional reliability, hybrid fuel efficiency, and World Rally Championship engineering, it is a giant of small-car motoring.

all_models.name: Ford Focus
all_models.overview: The Ford Focus replaced the Laser in 2002 and immediately established itself as Australia's benchmark dynamic driver's car in the compact segment thanks to its revolutionary 'Control Blade' multi-link rear suspension. Across four generations (LR, LT/LV, LW/LZ, and SA), the Focus earned critical acclaim. For Australian car enthusiasts, the Focus name was cemented by legendary performance flagships: the 2.0L high-revving LR ST170 (127 kW), the five-cylinder turbo LT/LV XR5 Turbo (166 kW 2.5L Volvo turbo) and limited-edition 224 kW Focus RS, the sensational 257 kW drift-mode AWD LZ Focus RS, and the nimble SA Focus ST.

all_models.name: Holden Barina
all_models.overview: For over 33 years across six generations, the Holden Barina was Australia's quintessential light car. Introduced in February 1985 as the MB Barina (a badge-engineered Suzuki Cultus made unforgettable by poet Pam Ayres' commercial: 'Beep beep, Barina!'), the model transitioned through the ML, MF, and MH series. In 1994, Holden pivoted to GM Europe with the SB Barina (Opel Corsa B), creating an Australian youth lifestyle phenomenon that produced the cult Barina GSi (1.6L 16V twin-cam). The 2001 XC Barina won Wheels Car of the Year 2001. Sourcing moved to GM Daewoo in 2005 with the value-focused TK, while the final 2011-2018 TM Barina featured GM's global Gamma II platform, culminating in the sporty Barina RS powered by a 103 kW 1.4L Turbo engine.

all_models.name: i30
all_models.overview: The Hyundai i30 is the vehicle that transformed Australian perceptions of the brand from budget-oriented to class-leading. Winner of the 2007 Wheels Car of the Year, it has been an Australian small car benchmark and gave rise to the sensational Albert Biermann-developed i30 N hot hatch.

all_models.name: XJ & XJ-S
all_models.vehicle_type: Large Luxury Sedan / Grand Tourer Coupe
all_models.overview: The apex of British automotive grandeur and motorsport glory. Sir William Lyons' XJ6 was declared the finest riding saloon in the world upon its Australian release, while the V12 XJ12 and XJ-S grand tourer achieved immortality when Tom Walkinshaw Racing's Jaguar XJS V12 conquered Mount Panorama to win the 1985 Bathurst 1000. Evolved through supercharged XJR flagships to the bonded-aluminium X350 and avant-garde X351.

all_models.name: CX-5
all_models.overview: The Mazda CX-5 is one of Australia's all-time most popular SUVs, holding the title of best-selling SUV in the country outright for multiple consecutive years. Debuting Mazda's SKYACTIV powertrain suite and Kodo 'Soul of Motion' design language, the CX-5 elevated the mid-size family crossover segment with class-leading steering feel, premium interiors, and punchy turbo power.

all_models.name: G-Class (Geländewagen)
all_models.overview: The immortal Mercedes-Benz Geländewagen. Originating as a relentless military off-roader with three locking differentials, the G-Class became a trusted explorer in the Australian outback and was selected by the Australian Defence Force under Project Overlander Land 121, resulting in over 2,000 bespoke Australian Army 4x4 and 6x6 vehicles. Concurrently, the civilian W463 morphed into the ultimate status symbol through the roaring twin-turbo V8 AMG G63.

all_models.name: Lancer Evolution & Ralliart
all_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution and Ralliart models represent one of the greatest chapters in modern Australian performance car folklore. Born directly from World Rally Championship battles where Tommi Mäkinen claimed four consecutive WRC drivers' titles, the Evo delivered staggering turbocharged all-wheel-drive grip, Active Yaw Control (AYC), and giant-killing cross-country pace.

all_models.name: Jimny / Sierra / Stockman
all_models.overview: The Suzuki Jimny, Sierra, and Stockman represent Australia's most revered lightweight, go-anywhere 4WD institution. Defying its miniature dimensions with a genuine ladder-frame chassis, dual-range transfer case, and live beam axles front and rear, it has conquered the Simpson Desert, Victorian High Country, and outback cattle stations for half a century.

all_models.name: Kluger
all_models.overview: The Toyota Kluger (sold globally as the Highlander) is Australia's quintessential car-based 7-seat family crossover SUV. Blending passenger-car ride comfort with cavernous interior room, powerful V6 and hybrid powertrains, and all-weather AWD assurance, it became a cornerstone of Australian suburban family motoring.

all_models.name: Polo
all_models.overview: Volkswagen's premium compact hatchback in Australia. Across four generations from the 6N to the modern MQB AW, the Polo brought big-car refinement, solid German safety, and pocket-rocket performance through the beloved Polo GTI.

all_models.name: Tiguan
all_models.overview: Volkswagen's powerhouse medium SUV in Australia, delivering European road manners, turbocharged TSI petrol and TDI diesel powertrains, 4Motion all-wheel drive, spacious 5-seat and 7-seat Allspace layouts, and the blisteringly fast 235kW Tiguan R.

all_models.name: Q5 & SQ5
all_models.overview: Audi's best-selling luxury SUV in Australia. Built on the longitudinal MLB platform with quattro permanent all-wheel drive, the Q5 balanced executive prestige with family versatility, while the twin-turbo diesel SQ5 BiTDI became an unprecedented cult sales sensation in Australia.

all_models.name: Ford Ranger
all_models.overview: The Ford Ranger is Australia's best-selling vehicle and one of the country's crowning engineering triumphs. Designed, engineered, and developed from the ground up by Ford Australia's 2,000-strong engineering and design team at Campbellfield, Victoria and the You Yangs Proving Ground, the Ranger is exported to over 180 countries. Across the PJ/PK, the revolutionary T6 (PX I, II, III), and the Next-Gen (PY), the Ranger redefined dual-cab refinement, off-road ability, and high-speed off-road performance through the bespoke Ranger Raptor.

all_models.name: Holden Captiva
all_models.overview: The Holden Captiva was Holden's core mid-size family SUV between 2006 and 2018, competing in Australia's exploding SUV segment against the Ford Territory and Toyota Kluger. Built on GM's global Theta platform, the range uniquely comprised two distinct body styles: the 5-seater Captiva 5 (Opel Antara twin) and the 7-seater Captiva 7 (Chevrolet Captiva). Over 150,000 Captivas found homes in Australian driveways thanks to keen pricing, standard three-row seating, AWD capability, and Australian-built Alloytec 3.2L and 3.0L SIDI V6 engines alongside 2.0L and 2.2L common-rail turbo diesels. Series II arrived in 2011 with refreshed styling, before the model was replaced by the Equinox and Acadia.

all_models.name: Holden Jackaroo
all_models.overview: The Holden Jackaroo (Isuzu Trooper / Bighorn) was Holden's frontline heavy-duty four-wheel-drive wagon from 1981 to 2004. Engineered to conquer the Australian outback, the Jackaroo competed directly against the Toyota LandCruiser Prado, Mitsubishi Pajero, and Nissan Patrol. The first-generation UBS-1 (1981-1992) offered short and long wheelbase bodies with rugged four-cylinder petrol and diesel engines. The second-generation UBS-2 (1992-2004) expanded into a wide-body luxury family 4WD featuring coil-sprung rear suspension, shift-on-the-fly 4WD, potent 3.2L and 3.5L DOHC 24V V6 petrol engines (158 kW), and advanced 3.0L 4JX1 common-rail turbo-diesel. The flagship Monterey added leather trim, woodgrain, climate control, and heated seats.

all_models.name: D-MAX
all_models.overview: The Isuzu D-MAX is an Australian commercial and recreational ute powerhouse. Renowned for its commercial truck-derived 3.0-litre 4JJ-series turbo diesel engine, 3,500kg braked towing capacity, and unbreakable durability, the D-MAX grew from an independent newcomer in 2008 into the third best-selling vehicle outright in Australia.

all_models.name: Grand Cherokee
all_models.overview: The American flagship that revolutionized Australia's large SUV market. Across five generations (ZJ, WJ, WK, WK2, and WL), the Grand Cherokee blended authentic Jeep trail capability with luxury appointments, muscular HEMI V8s, efficient 3.0L diesels with 3,500kg towing, and the earth-shattering 522kW Grand Cherokee Trackhawk.

all_models.name: Range Rover & Discovery
all_models.overview: The twin benchmarks of British luxury and all-terrain expedition mastery in Australia. The Range Rover created the luxury 4WD genre in 1972, proving that supreme off-road capability could coexist with peerless aristocratic comfort. The Land Rover Discovery launched in Australia in 1991, democratizing Range Rover technology into an iconic stepped-roof, 7-seat family adventurer.

all_models.name: RX-3 / 808
all_models.overview: The Mazda RX-3 (Savanna) and its reciprocating-piston sister the Mazda 808 (Grand Familia) are iconic pillars of Australian motorsport history and Japanese performance folklore. Famed for taking the fight directly to Holden Torana GTR XU-1s and Ford Falcon GT-HOs at Mount Panorama Bathurst, the RX-3's screaming twin-rotor Wankel rotary engine won legions of fanatical followers.

all_models.name: Starion & Cordia Turbo
all_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Starion Turbo and Cordia GSR Turbo were the trailblazers of Japanese factory turbocharging in 1980s Australia. From the front-wheel drive Cordia GSR with its mind-bending 'Super Shift' 4x2 twin-stick dual-range transmission to the widebody, rear-wheel drive Starion Turbo that battled Australian Touring Cars in Group E and Group A, these coupes created Australia's turbo street-racing legend.

all_models.name: Triton
all_models.overview: The Mitsubishi Triton has been one of Australia's favourite dual-cab utes for over four decades, offering tough ladder-chassis capability, advanced Super Select II 4WD, and exceptional value for trades and families.

all_models.name: Cayenne & Macan
all_models.overview: The commercial lifeblood of modern Porsche. When introduced in 2003, the Cayenne proved that a true Porsche could haul five adults and conquer the Simpson Desert, while setting racetrack lap records. The smaller Macan arrived in 2014, quickly becoming Porsche's best-selling model in Australia, and leading Porsche's electric transformation with the Macan EV.

all_models.name: Amarok
all_models.overview: Volkswagen's rugged mid-size commercial pickup truck, celebrated in Australia for full-time 4Motion all-wheel drive, class-leading tub width capable of carrying a full-sized Australian pallet between the wheel arches, and powerhouse 3.0-litre V6 TDI engines developed with Walkinshaw Automotive (W580).

all_models.name: Giulia Sprint GT, GTV & Giulia Quadrifoglio
all_models.overview: The passionate soul of Italian motoring in Australia. Spanning from the Bertone-styled 105 Series Giulia Sprint GT and Bathurst-winning 1750/2000 GTV, through the transaxle Alfetta GTV6 Group A touring car, to the spine-tingling Busso V6 156 GTA and the modern Giorgio-platform Giulia Quadrifoglio with its Ferrari-derived 375kW twin-turbo V6.

all_models.name: 500 & Abarth 595/695
all_models.overview: The Italian style icon that charmed Australia. From the original rear-engined 500 'Bambino' that motorized post-war migrants and Australian urbanites, to the retro-chic 2008 rebirth (Typ 312) and the scorpion-badged Abarth 595 and 695 hot hatches with screaming Record Monza exhausts and Brembo brakes.

all_models.name: Ford Everest
all_models.overview: While built at AutoAlliance Thailand in Rayong, the Ford Everest was conceived, designed, engineered, and durability-tested in Australia by Ford's 2,000-strong global product development hub at Campbellfield and the You Yangs Proving Ground. Developed concurrently with the Ranger ute, the Everest transformed the T6 ladder-frame architecture into a refined 7-seat family wagon featuring coil-sprung Watt's linkage rear suspension, electronic terrain management, and 3.1-tonne towing. The 2015 UA series launched with the rugged 3.2L 5-cylinder Duratorq turbo-diesel and later 2.0L Bi-Turbo with 10-speed auto. The 2022+ UB Next-Gen Everest elevated the platform into an opulent, class-leading 4WD with standard 3.5-tonne towing and a flagship 3.0L V6 Turbo Diesel producing 184 kW and 600 Nm.

all_models.name: Wrangler
all_models.overview: The direct descendant of the WWII Willys military Jeep, celebrated in Australia for live beam axles, removable doors and roof, fold-flat windscreen, and rock-crawling Rubicon mastery across TJ, JK, and JL generations.

all_models.name: T60 & eT60
all_models.overview: The Chinese 1-tonne ute that disrupted the Australian market. Debuting in 2017 as the first Chinese-manufactured vehicle to achieve a 5-star ANCAP safety rating, the LDV T60 delivered unmatched equipment-for-price value. The 2021 T60 Max raised the stakes with a class-leading 160kW/500Nm 2.0L Bi-Turbo diesel, while the 2022 eT60 became Australia's first commercially available electric factory ute.

all_models.name: RX-7
all_models.overview: The Mazda RX-7 is a rotary-powered sports car legend with deep Australian motorsport roots. From Allan Moffat's ATCC championship and Bathurst battles in the 1980s to Mazda Motorsport's Australian-exclusive RX-7 SP winning the Bathurst 12 Hour in 1995.

all_models.name: C-Class
all_models.overview: Mercedes-Benz's most popular luxury nameplate in Australia, spanning W202, W203, W204, W205, and W206. Renowned for supreme safety engineering, quiet cabin isolation, and thundering naturally aspirated and biturbo V8 AMG performance flagships.

all_models.name: ZS / ZST / MG4
all_models.overview: The modern pillars of MG Motor's Australian volume resurgence under SAIC: the top-selling ZS and turbocharged ZST compact SUVs, the trailblazing ZS EV, and the universally acclaimed rear-wheel-drive MG4 electric hatchback (including the 320kW XPower).

all_models.name: Pajero
all_models.overview: With 12 victories in the grueling Dakar Rally, the Mitsubishi Pajero is one of the world's most successful four-wheel drives. In Australia, it defined the family 4WD wagon for nearly four decades across four generations.

all_models.name: 205, 306, 208 & 308 GTi
all_models.overview: The aristocrats of French hot hatch engineering. For more than three decades in Australia, Peugeot's GTi lineage defined what a front-wheel drive performance car could achieve. From the featherweight, razor-sharp 205 GTi 1.9 that reset international benchmarks, through the passive rear-steering 306 GTi-6 with its class-first six-speed manual, to the Peugeot Sport-engineered 308 GTi 270 with Torsen LSD and massive Alcon brakes.

all_models.name: Jumbuck & Satria (including Satria GTi)
all_models.overview: The cult Malaysian heroes of Australian roads. The Proton Satria GTi became an instant hot hatch sensation in 1999, engineered with genuine Lotus suspension wizardry, Recaro bucket seats, riveted widebody arch flares, and a twin-cam Mitsubishi engine. Alongside it, the Proton Jumbuck carved out a unique niche from 2003 as Australia's most affordable brand-new ute, offering compact car economy with a half-tonne payload.

all_models.name: Clio RS & Megane RS (Renault Sport)
all_models.overview: The front-wheel-drive Nurburgring lap record conquerors. Developed by the wizards of Renault Sport at Dieppe, the Clio RS and Megane RS established an unbeatable pedigree in Australia for pure driving dynamics, PerfoHub independent steering axis suspension, mechanical limited-slip differentials, and Brembo stopping power.

Born from jets. Saab brought Swedish aircraft engineering, wraparound windscreens, night panels, and turbocharging mastery to Australia across more than three decades. The Classic 900 Turbo established Saab's intellectual cool, followed by the lightning-quick 9-3 Viggen and the 206kW 2.8T Aero V6.

all_models.name: Octavia
all_models.overview: The intelligent family choice in Australia. Since spearheading Skoda's return to Australia in October 2007, the Octavia has won legions of loyal fans by combining Volkswagen Group engineering and Golf GTI drivetrains with cavernous boot space and 'Simply Clever' practical details. The Octavia RS Liftback and Combi wagon represent Australia's favorite value performance family express.

all_models.name: Model 3
all_models.overview: The electric vehicle that opened the floodgates for mass EV adoption in Australia. Built in Shanghai for the Australian market, the Model 3 transformed automotive sales by outselling traditional petrol luxury sedans like the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes C-Class.

all_models.name: RAV4
all_models.overview: The Toyota RAV4 created the compact car-based recreational SUV category in 1994. Across five generations, it grew into Australia's favourite SUV, with the XA50 Hybrid triggering unprecedented multi-month waitlists.

all_models.name: Shark 6 / Atto 3 / Seal
all_models.overview: The trio of game-changing vehicles that propelled BYD to electric and hybrid leadership in Australia: the Atto 3 compact SUV, the Seal sports sedan, and the groundbreaking Shark 6 plug-in hybrid dual-cab ute with 321kW.

all_models.name: Cannon / Haval H6 / Tank 300
all_models.overview: The full evolution of Great Wall Motor in Australia: beginning with the pioneering 2009 Great Wall V240 and V200 utes, progressing to the top-selling GWM Cannon dual-cab, high-tech Haval H6 Hybrid SUV, and heavy-duty Tank 300 off-roader.

all_models.name: Stinger
all_models.overview: The Kia Stinger arrived in Australia in late 2017 just as Holden and Ford ceased local manufacturing, instantly becoming the spiritual successor to the rear-wheel-drive Falcon and Commodore. Powered by a 272kW twin-turbo V6, it was adopted by Australian police forces as a high-speed pursuit interceptor.

all_models.name: BT-50
all_models.overview: The Mazda BT-50 has been an Australian tradie, touring, and towing mainstay across three generations, moving from a Ford Ranger twin with 3.2L 5-cylinder power to an Isuzu D-Max platform with the 3.0L 4JJ3 turbo-diesel.

all_models.name: Model Y
all_models.overview: Australia's top-selling electric SUV and one of the highest-selling SUVs outright in Australia. Built on the Model 3 platform with a taller crossover body, 2,158 litres of total cargo storage, and class-leading electrical efficiency.

all_models.name: 86 / GR86
all_models.overview: The Toyota 86 and GR86 re-energized accessible rear-wheel-drive sports motoring in Australia. Developed jointly with Subaru (who built the cars at the Gunma Main Plant), the 86 combined a low center of gravity boxer engine, lightweight chassis, razor-sharp steering, and rear-drive dynamics at an accessible price point.

all_models.name: Holden Colorado
all_models.overview: The Holden Colorado was Holden's rugged 4x4 and 4x2 dual-cab, space-cab, and single-cab workhorse pick-up, replacing the legendary Rodeo in 2008. Across the RC and RG generations, the Colorado delivered class-leading 3.5-tonne braked towing capacity and up to 500Nm of torque from its Duramax 2.8L turbo-diesel engine. In 2016, Holden's engineering team at Lang Lang conducted a massive Australian-specific chassis, steering, and powertrain calibration that transformed refinement and dynamics.

all_models.name: Giulia
all_models.overview: The quintessential sports sedan across classic 105 series and modern Giorgio-platform Type 952 with 50:50 weight balance.

all_models.name: 105 GTV / Spider
all_models.overview: Bertone-designed Giulia Sprint GT, 1750 GTV, and Pininfarina Spider; revered collector cars in Australia.

all_models.name: Stelvio
all_models.overview: Alfa Romeo's first production SUV, sharing the Giorgio architecture and steering sharpness of the Giulia.

all_models.name: A110
all_models.overview: Ultralight mid-engine aluminium two-seater sports car, powered by a 1.8-litre turbocharged four-cylinder with 7-speed Getrag wet dual-clutch.

all_models.name: DB9 / DB11 / DB12
all_models.overview: The core V12 and twin-turbo grand tourer lineage, marrying aluminum structure with spine-tingling British pace.

all_models.name: Vantage
all_models.overview: Aston Martin's pure driver's sports car, spanning dry-sump 4.3L/4.7L V8, manic V12 Vantage, and modern 489kW twin-turbo warrior.

all_models.name: A4
all_models.overview: Audi's core luxury sedan and Avant wagon, pioneering quattro all-wheel drive in the compact executive class across B5 through B9.

all_models.name: Q5
all_models.overview: Audi's top-selling vehicle in Australia, revered by families for its refined quattro dynamics, TDI torque, and high-performance SQ5 variant.

all_models.name: RS6 Avant
all_models.overview: The ultimate high-performance family supercar wagon in Australia, featuring twin-turbo V8 and V10 power with quattro traction.

all_models.name: Continental GT
all_models.overview: The definitive modern Bentley, combining hand-stitched leather, knurled metal, and thunderous twin-turbo W12 and V8 engines.

all_models.name: 5 Series
all_models.overview: BMW's executive express, defining executive sports saloons from E12 and E28 through E39 and modern G60.

all_models.name: M3
all_models.overview: The iconic high-performance sports benchmark in Australia with ATCC championship victories and high-revving motorsport powertrains.

all_models.name: Dolphin
all_models.overview: One of Australia's most affordable new electric cars, delivering high five-star ANCAP safety and ocean-inspired styling.

all_models.name: Lyriq
all_models.overview: Cadillac's debut electric SUV in Australia, featuring 102kWh Ultium battery, 373kW dual-motor AWD, and a 33-inch curved LED 9K display.

all_models.name: Seven
all_models.overview: Lightweight open-wheel roadster weighing just 500-600kg, offering unmatched cornering G-forces and mechanical feedback.

all_models.name: Omoda 5 / Omoda E5
all_models.overview: Chery's comeback hero in Australia, featuring diamond-pattern grille, dual 10.25-inch screens, five-star ANCAP safety, and all-electric E5.

all_models.name: Tiggo 7 Pro & Tiggo 8 Pro Max
all_models.overview: Value-packed family SUVs offering panoramic sunroofs, Sony audio, and 2.0-litre turbo all-wheel drive.

all_models.name: Corvette C8
all_models.overview: The first factory right-hand drive Corvette in history, bringing mid-engine exotic performance and naturally aspirated V8 roar to Australian dealerships.

all_models.name: Chrysler Scorpion
all_models.overview: Stylish 2-door pillarless sports coupe based on the Mitsubishi Sapporo, offering luxury grand-touring features.

all_models.name: Chrysler 300C
all_models.overview: Brawny American rear-wheel-drive luxury sedan with gangsta proportions, packing 5.7L Hemi V8 and 6.4L SRT-8 performance.

all_models.name: Chrysler PT Cruiser
all_models.overview: Retro-styled multi-purpose hatchback inspired by 1930s American hot rods, featuring versatile seating and cabriolet option.

all_models.name: Chrysler Crossfire
all_models.overview: Striking German-built sports car manufactured by Karmann in Osnabruck, sharing 80% of its components with the Mercedes-Benz SLK (R170).

all_models.name: Chrysler Voyager / Grand Voyager
all_models.overview: The pioneer of the modern minivan, offering Stow 'n Go fold-into-the-floor seating and power sliding doors across GS, RG, and RT generations.

all_models.name: Chrysler Sebring
all_models.overview: American mid-size car offered in four-door sedan and two-door cabriolet featuring a three-piece folding steel hardtop.

all_models.name: Chrysler Neon
all_models.overview: Cab-forward American compact car with perky performance from its standard 2.0L 16-valve engine.

all_models.name: C5 / C5 X
all_models.overview: Flagship French cruiser featuring Hydractive III+ suspension and culminating in the innovative C5 X crossover fastback.

all_models.name: Formentor
all_models.overview: Cupra's bespoke crossover coupe, combining striking copper accents with 228kW all-wheel drive performance.

all_models.name: Born
all_models.overview: Cupra's first all-electric hot hatch in Australia, featuring rear-wheel drive and up to 170kW e-Boost performance.

all_models.name: Lanos
all_models.overview: Giugiaro-styled light car, a top-selling budget runabout with Daewoo's 3-year Free Care package.

all_models.name: Matiz
all_models.overview: Tiny 5-door city runabout styled by Italdesign Giugiaro, offering 5-door versatility in a sub-3.5m length.

all_models.name: Nubira
all_models.overview: Spacious compact car engineered in the UK and styled by I.DE.A Institute in Italy.
